title: Wall Street’s Hottest AI Stock Trade Isn’t Buying AI. It’s Buying Protection From It
description:
Cybersecurity stocks surged on November 18 as investors bet on defense against AI hacking, a threat crypto knows.
The post Wall Street’s Hottest AI Stock Trade Isn’t Buying AI. It’s Buying Protection From It appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Cybersecurity stocks were the standout of the November 18 session. The move echoes a September rally that Dow Jones tied to the debate over artificial intelligence (AI) risks.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and CrowdStrike (CRWD) rose substantially as the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.13%. However, Palo Alto then reported earnings after the bell, and its shares fell on guidance.

Are Cybersecurity Stocks Pricing In AI Fear?

Yahoo Finance’s top U.S. gainers list on November 19 showed 15 of 25 names were security or network infrastructure firms.

Palo Alto reported that next-generation security annual recurring revenue jumped 66% to $9.73 billion. It raised full-year profit guidance, yet shares still fell afterward.

The company also authorized a $1 billion buyback through 2027, equal to 0.36% of its market value.

Palo Alto also announced plans to acquire Applied Compute. The deal targets secure open-weight AI models, which publish their trained parameters, for enterprise customers.

Palo Alto chief executive Nikesh Arora said in September that awareness of weaponized AI is growing. Dow Jones reported that OpenAI models breached Hugging Face, an AI company, adding urgency to the debate.

Results from other security vendors could show how much of the rally reflects AI fear rather than earnings.

Has Crypto Already Felt the Threat?

April 2026 crypto hacks drained more than $606 million from protocols in the first 18 days of the month. That made it the worst month for exploits since February 2025.

Whether AI drove those losses, however, remains contested. Wasabi Protocol, a Decentralized Finance (DeFi) platform, lost over $5 million to an admin-key compromise.

The AI-driven DeFi hacker theory resurfaced, though on-chain security firm Blockaid traced the breach to one admin wallet.

Drift Protocol and KelpDAO, the two biggest April hacks, totaled $577 million. Neither was a code exploit, according to a review of 2026 DeFi losses.

Meanwhile, equity investors bid up security stocks while crypto still debates whether AI is behind its losses. DeFi total value locked, the capital deposited in protocols, had fallen 39% in 2026 by late June.

The post Wall Street’s Hottest AI Stock Trade Isn’t Buying AI. It’s Buying Protection From It appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Anthropic reportedly prices blockbuster IPO at $83 a share ahead of public trading
description:
Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) will price its IPO at $83 per share, ahead of its Thursday trading debut, according to Bloomberg. That's above earlier estimates of $80.  The outlet previously reported that shares were oversubscribed by as much as 6x.
Anthropic, which Yahoo Finance named its Company of the Year for 2026, reported in its most recent amended S-1 that its third-quarter  revenue climbed to $17 billion, a 12x year over year increase.
For the nine months that ended Sept. 30, Anthropic's sales eclipsed $33 billion. It brought in $2.5 billion in all of 2025 and just $41 million in 2023.
Anthropic's sales continue to improve. Its number of customers spending more than $100,000 has increased from roughly 1,500 in December 2025 to more than 11,900 as of Sept. 30. Its computing efficiency has also jumped, meaning it's seeing more revenue per dollar spent on computing infrastructure.
"There's no real historical analogy for a company that has been this successful this fast," NYU Stern School of Business professor Arun Sundararajan told Yahoo Finance.
Anthropic's public debut also comes amid a wave of upheaval in the AI industry, ranging from market jitters to questions about the technology's impact on jobs.
It also faces plenty of competition from rival OpenAI (OPAI.PVT), as well as heavy hitters like Google (GOOG, GOOGL) and Meta (META).
Now the market will determine how that risk factors into the company's future prospects.


This article originally appeared on Yahoo Finance at https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/live/anthropic-ipo-live-company-said-to-price-stock-at-83-begin-trading-thursday-212656452.html

title: If You Invested $100 in Bitcoin When Rockstar First Confirmed GTA 6, Here’s How Much You’d Have Today
description:
$100 in Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) on the day Rockstar first confirmed GTA 6 would be worth $154.70 now, as the game rolls out worldwide this week.
The Wild Ride While Fans Waited
Rockstar told fans on Feb. 4, 2022, that "the next entry in the Grand Theft Auto series is well underway," back when Bitcoin traded at $41,500. 
That $100 bought about 0.0024 BTC, and the ride from there was rough. By Nov. 21, 2022, deep in that year’s crypto winter, Bitcoin had sunk below $16,000, shrinking the position to just $38.04.
It took until Rockstar’s December 2023 trailer reveal, when the game was formally named Grand Theft Auto VI, for the position to crawl back above its starting value, hitting $101.15 as Bitcoin traded near $41,980. 
The real payoff came later: by Oct. 6, 2025, with Bitcoin near its then-record high above $124,000, the same $100 was worth $300.60. 
It has since given back more than half of that, landing at $154.70, or a 54.7% gain, as Bitcoin trades around $64,200 and GTA VI rolls out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S starting Nov. 19. 
Players in New Zealand, where launch day arrived first, already had access as of midnight local time, Reuters reported.
That’s still enough to cover the game’s $79.99 standard edition with $74.71 left over before tax.
What If You’d Waited for the Trailers Instead?
The two trailer dates would have produced very different outcomes:
First trailer, Dec. 4, 2023: Bitcoin traded at $41,980.10 when Rockstar revealed the game’s title. A $100 purchase then would be worth $152.93 today, just $1.77 less than buying nearly 22 months earlier when Rockstar first confirmed the game was in development.
Second trailer, May 6, 2025: Bitcoin traded at $96,802.48 when that trailer dropped. A $100 purchase then would be worth only $66.32 now, leaving the buyer $13.67 short of the game’s $79.99 standard edition before tax.
Image: Shutterstock

title: PlayStation Network plagued with service disruptions as gamers await 'GTA 6' release
description:
As users prepared their consoles for the new Grand Theft Auto VI, website outage tracker Downdetector was showing a sharp spike in outages across the PlayStation Network on Wednesday. 
Users reported seeing "services are busy" when they tried to sign in to their consoles. Sony needs to verify that a game like GTA 6 was legitimately purchased before one can download it, and verification requires an internet connection. An outage like this could prevent players who pre-ordered the title from downloading and accessing it immediately at launch.
PlayStation didn't immediately reply to a request for comment, but its status page was showing all services up and running in the U.S. Wednesday afternoon by 4 p.m. ET. An earlier message on the page alerted users to a possible issue: "You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience," the notice read.
By 5 p.m. ET, the outage seemed to have come down from its peak although some users were still reporting issues.
GTA6 is set to go live at midnight local time, so users in New Zealand were first to be able to play. The game clocks in at a whopping 212GB, and was already Metacritic's highest-rated video game ever  only a few hours into the launch.
Some users in other time zones attempted to set their console's region to New Zealand to get in on the game early, but the process on PS5 is more involved than on Xbox. Plus, PlayStation announced Wednesday that before users could play the game, a software update was necessary.  A few users who had tried the time zone workaround reported their accounts had been banned
The outage comes on the heels of several other major internet outages over the past week, that included Apple iCloud, Microsoft, several banks and an FAA full ground stop of all air travel in the U.S. last Friday. There's still no indication that any of the outages are connected, but wary internet denizens wondered if AI could be to blame.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo Tech at https://tech.yahoo.com/gaming/breaking-news/article/playstation-network-down-for-thousands-as-gta-6-launches-204149781.html

title: Anthropic Prices IPO At $83, Above Range, In What Could Be Biggest Listing Ever (UPDATED)
description:
Editor’s note: This story has been updated with Anthropic’s $83-per-share IPO price; an earlier version reported only the expected price range.
Anthropic has priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above the $70-to-$78 range it marketed to investors, according to people familiar with the matter cited by CNBC and Bloomberg, a day before the stock is set to make its highly anticipated Nasdaq debut.
With the higher price, the IPO is expected to raise at least $68 billion, Bloomberg reported. 
CNBC said that if all 825 million shares originally planned are sold, the offering would bring in about $68.5 billion. Adding the $26 billion that investors including Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) agreed to invest at the IPO price, the total would come to more than $94 billion, the largest IPO on record.
That would top SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in June with its base IPO offering, or $86.2 billion including the over-allotment option. 
Anthropic had marketed a base offering of 801.4 million shares, while selling investors offered 23.6 million shares, according to its filings. Bloomberg reported the size of the offering has increased, which could lift the final total. 
Goldman Sachs Group Inc. (NYSE:GS) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) are leading the offering, with 20 other banks participating. Shares are expected to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, making Anthropic the first frontier AI lab to go public — ahead of rival OpenAI, which isn’t planning a listing before 2027.
Wall Street Sees The Listing As A Catalyst
At HSBC, the deal is framed as a possible turning point for a battered tech trade. Analysts still read it that way after a week in which Nvidia was hit by the departure of Jensen Huang.
“The upcoming Anthropic IPO is the likely next positive catalyst for equities, in our view,” Max Kettner, HSBC’s chief multi-asset strategist, wrote in a Monday note.
“This week’s Anthropic IPO could well be the next bullish catalyst for tech given likely more reasonable valuations,” the note added. 
It also warned that “it’s very unlikely that even a successful IPO will finally lead to a more ‘trending’ market.”
At $83, Anthropic lists below Morningstar‘s fair value estimate of $92 per share, or about $1.7 trillion. 
That estimate assumes 47% annual revenue growth over five years. Morningstar’s bull case is $188 a share and its bear case is $25, with a “Very High” uncertainty rating.
Prediction Markets Are Scaling Back
Traders on Polymarket are lowering their expectations for the debut.
In the market on Anthropic’s closing market cap on its first trading day, the $1.25 trillion-to-$1.5 trillion bracket leads at 44.5%. That is up 6.5 percentage points in the past day. 
The odds of a close below $1.25 trillion have risen 18.9 points in a week, to 39.1%.
The odds of a close above $1.5 trillion have dropped to 19.9%, down 24.3 points in a week. The $1.75 trillion-to-$2 trillion bracket has fallen to 3.4%. The event has drawn more than $11.2 million in volume.




From $41 Million To $16 Billion In Three Years
The prospectus shows how fast revenue has grown.
Anthropic reported $41 million in revenue in 2023, its first commercial year. That rose to $386 million in 2024, up about 842%. In 2025, revenue reached $4.59 billion, an increase of about 1,088% from a year earlier.
Growth has not slowed in 2026. Revenue hit $16.3 billion in the first six months of the year, compared with $1.16 billion a year earlier. That is about 14 times as much, and about 3.5 times Anthropic’s revenue for all of 2025. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, revenue reached $33.24 billion, up roughly 1,200% from a year earlier, according to the prospectus.
The prospectus says revenue grew 1,368% year over year in the three months ended June 30, 2026, to about $11.6 billion. That was up 144% from the first quarter.

Editor’s note: This story has been updated with Anthropic’s $83-per-share IPO price; an earlier version reported only the expected price range.

Anthropic has priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above the $70-to-$78 range it marketed to investors, according to people familiar with the matter cited by CNBC and Bloomberg, a day before the stock is set to make its highly anticipated Nasdaq debut.

With the higher price, the IPO is expected to raise at least $68 billion, Bloomberg reported.

CNBC said that if all 825 million shares originally planned are sold, the offering would bring in about $68.5 billion. Adding the $26 billion that investors including Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) agreed to invest at the IPO price, the total would come to more than $94 billion, the largest IPO on record.

That would top SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in June with its base IPO offering, or $86.2 billion including the over-allotment option.

Anthropic had marketed a base offering of 801.4 million shares, while selling investors offered 23.6 million shares, according to its filings. Bloomberg reported the size of the offering has increased, which could lift the final total.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc. (NYSE:GS) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) are leading the offering, with 20 other banks participating. Shares are expected to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, making Anthropic the first frontier AI lab to go public — ahead of rival OpenAI, which isn’t planning a listing before 2027.

Wall Street Sees The Listing As A Catalyst

At HSBC, the deal is framed as a possible turning point for a battered tech trade. Analysts still read it that way after a week in which Nvidia was hit by the departure of Jensen Huang.

“The upcoming Anthropic IPO is the likely next positive catalyst for equities, in our view,” Max Kettner, HSBC’s chief multi-asset strategist, wrote in a Monday note.

“This week’s Anthropic IPO could well be the next bullish catalyst for tech given likely more reasonable valuations,” the note added.

It also warned that “it’s very unlikely that even a successful IPO will finally lead to a more ‘trending’ market.”

At $83, Anthropic lists below Morningstar‘s fair value estimate of $92 per share, or about $1.7 trillion.

That estimate assumes 47% annual revenue growth over five years. Morningstar’s bull case is $188 a share and its bear case is $25, with a “Very High” uncertainty rating.

Prediction Markets Are Scaling Back

Traders on Polymarket are lowering their expectations for the debut.

In the market on Anthropic’s closing market cap on its first trading day, the $1.25 trillion-to-$1.5 trillion bracket leads at 44.5%. That is up 6.5 percentage points in the past day.

The odds of a close below $1.25 trillion have risen 18.9 points in a week, to 39.1%.

The odds of a close above $1.5 trillion have dropped to 19.9%, down 24.3 points in a week. The $1.75 trillion-to-$2 trillion bracket has fallen to 3.4%. The event has drawn more than $11.2 million in volume.

From $41 Million To $16 Billion In Three Years

The prospectus shows how fast revenue has grown.

Anthropic reported $41 million in revenue in 2023, its first commercial year. That rose to $386 million in 2024, up about 842%. In 2025, revenue reached $4.59 billion, an increase of about 1,088% from a year earlier.

Growth has not slowed in 2026. Revenue hit $16.3 billion in the first six months of the year, compared with $1.16 billion a year earlier. That is about 14 times as much, and about 3.5 times Anthropic’s revenue for all of 2025. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, revenue reached $33.24 billion, up roughly 1,200% from a year earlier, according to the prospectus.

The prospectus says revenue grew 1,368% year over year in the three months ended June 30, 2026, to about $11.6 billion. That was up 144% from the first quarter.

Compute and infrastructure expenses grew 300% over the same period. That gap between revenue growth and cost growth is the core of the bull case.

Customers Are Spending Much More

Anthropic says its net revenue retention was about 900% as of Sept. 30, 2026. In other words, existing customers spent roughly nine times more than a year earlier.

Customers generating more than $100,000 in trailing 12-month revenue rose to more than 11,900, up from about 950 a year earlier.

The losses are also large. Anthropic reported an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of 2026, compared with about $42 billion for all of 2025.

That leaves the question Wall Street will start answering Thursday. Investors can see the growth in the numbers. What they are paying $83 a share for is how long it lasts.

title: S&P 500 Breaks Critical Support: Is a Bigger Stock Market Crash Coming?
description:
The S&P 500 lost its 200-day moving average. Historical data, hedging, and key chart levels hint at what comes next.
The post S&P 500 Breaks Critical Support: Is a Bigger Stock Market Crash Coming? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
The S&P 500 has fallen below one of Wall Street’s most closely watched warning levels, raising fears that the stock market correction could deepen.

The index dropped to 7,323 on Tuesday, closing below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April 7. It is now 6.4% below October’s record high.

Even Nvidia’s stronger-than-expected earnings have failed to settle the bigger concern: whether the AI-driven stock market rally is losing momentum.

History Suggests the S&P 500 Could Fall Further

Market research firm Bluekurtic found a troubling historical pattern.

Although the S&P 500 closed below its 200-day average, the SPY ETF recovered enough to finish slightly above its own.

Since 1993, this has happened 11 times. In 10 cases, SPY fell further within the following 10 trading sessions. The average maximum decline was 4.2%.

“It feels premature to call today as a bottom in the S&P 500.”

However, the median 10-day return was just -0.3%, suggesting that previous selloffs often stabilized relatively quickly.

Another indicator, the Zweig Breadth Thrust, has entered an early setup phase. All 17 confirmed signals since 1950 preceded higher markets six and 12 months later.

However, fewer than 2% of setups become confirmed signals.

Traders Are Preparing for More Volatility

The Cboe one-day volatility index surged 35.7% to 26.84 on Tuesday, reflecting expectations of a roughly 1.7% market move in either direction.

Trader Klarck warns that weakening market participation is leaving the S&P 500 increasingly dependent on technology giants.

He believes Anthropic’s November 19 IPO could mark a peak in AI enthusiasm, although that remains speculative.

For investors, 7,345 is the immediate level to watch. Reclaiming that moving average could support a recovery. 

Further weakness would put the 7,240 support area in focus, increasing the risk of a deeper correction.

title: $3 Million in Crypto, Gone Out of Reach, All Because of One Mistake
description: Two addresses flagged as scam-linked reportedly belong to Merlin Chain's bridge, which remains unlabeled in many blockchain compliance tools.
fullContent:
Blockchain investigator ZachXBT has accused Indian law enforcement of wrongly freezing approximately $3 million worth of BTC belonging to a Chinese crypto investor.

This is after they mistook transactions involving the Merlin Chain bridge for funds linked to a pig butchering scam.

Merlin Chain Bridge Mistaken for Scam-Linked Address

In an investigation published on November 18, ZachXBT traced the dispute to a May 2025 pig butchering case, where a victim identified as Andhra Pradesh allegedly lost $1.7 million in BTC, USDT, DOGE, and SOL.

The victim reported the incident to the criminal investigation department, which filed a charge sheet in March this year.

Then in July 2025, the Chinese investor, who goes by “Keym” on X, moved 15 BTC from an address, 3NcBhqK, to a deposit address on Gate, with the crypto exchange then freezing that account days later. At the time, it held about $3 million worth of crypto, although its remaining balance right now is worth around $1.5 million to $1.6 million because of declines in the value of the assets.

That freezing, according to ZachXBT, was due to a labeling error. He noted that shortly before the Gate deposit, a wallet controlled by Keym received funds from two addresses tagged as alibart[.]bit, which Indian police had identified as being associated with the scam that Pradesh had been a victim of.

However, per the analyst’s investigations, both addresses are part of the Merlin Chain bridge infrastructure, which most compliance tools often leave unlabeled.

According to the investigator, Keym is an ordinary user of Merlin, and transaction records tie three Merlin withdrawals between March and June 2025 to payouts from those bridge addresses, with the funds coming out of 50 BTC Keym bridged into Merlin on March 28, 2024. That’s more than a year before the alleged theft, and the analyst found no on-chain link to the victim’s losses.

Pressure on Exchanges and Police

On their part, Keym recounted how Gate had requested documentation shortly after their July 2025 deposit, but even after repeated submissions, the restriction on the account was not resolved. The user’s lawyers also reportedly requested transaction evidence connecting their holdings to the stolen funds, but apparently, investigators never provided the requested chain of transactions.

ZachXBT called the handling of the case “embarrassing incompetence,” adding that Indian law enforcement “seems incapable of reviewing basic blockchain data.”

“Indian LE, the prosecutor and the judge all signed off on this, Gate froze the account, and LE did a full press release about it recently, while the real victim here (the Gate user) hasn’t had access to his funds for nearly 16 months,” he wrote.

The sleuth has been busy, having earlier this month flagged a suspected theft of at least $133 million worth of crypto from several CEX accounts linked to French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa.

The post $3 Million in Crypto, Gone Out of Reach, All Because of One Mistake appeared first on CryptoPotato.

title: Variational Hits $1.5B Valuation in $110M Round to Take on Robinhood and IBKR
description:
Crypto trading startup Variational raised $110 million at a $1.5 billion valuation in the Series B round to compete with brokerages like Robinhood Markets Inc. and Interactive Brokers LLC. 
The financing round was led by Bain Capital Crypto, an early-stage crypto-native fund, where Stefan Cohen is a partner.  Other participants included Dragonfly Capital, HSG and Peak XV. 
“They’re [Variational] basically plugging into all of these off-chain liquidity sources and innovating on this broker model that they’ve established,” said Stefan Cohen.
 Crypto Startup with Traditional Finance Ambitions 
Variational is a derivatives trading protocol registered in the Cayman Islands that lets users trade swaps and perpetuals for both crypto and traditional assets, including stocks, commodities and pre-IPO equities. 
The company reports over 100,000 accounts and more than $475 billion in trading volume processed since launching the trading platform in 2025. 
Variational operates on a brokerage model, routing trades to and from crypto protocols and centralised trading venues, with over half of the platform's daily volume now on traditional markets. 
Unlike other on-chain trading platforms, Variational aggregates liquidity from both traditional and on-chain markets, making this dual approach integral to its strategy.
“I think there’s a place for both of us in the ecosystem, especially because again, we’re building just a very different type of product for TradFi trading,” said Variational chief executive officer Lucas Schuermann. 
While the platform is often viewed as a Hyperliquid rival, Schuermann said they're setting their sights on brokerages like Robinhood Markets Inc. and Interactive Brokers LLC. 
The company plans to invest the raised capital in strengthening the traditional part of its ecosystem: scaling swap markets, launching a public trading API, and moving swaps toward 24/7 trading. 
The Perpetual Boom Meets a Fractured Regulatory Environment
  Perpetuals are the latest and the hottest trend in the global finance ecosystem. In October, Intercontinental Exchange Inc. invested in Trade [XYZ], which deploys perpetuals for traditional assets on Hyperliquid. 
In November 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in the US allowed perpetual futures on single stocks could begin trading on regulated U.S. exchanges, subject to joint CFTC and SEC oversight. 
In the EU, perpetuals are not explicitly banned for retail traders, but regulators may treat them as derivatives. In the UK, it is strictly forbidden to offer crypto derivatives to retail traders. 
Meanwhile, Variational’s services are not available in the US, Canada and several other prohibited jurisdictions. EU and UK citizens are not excluded, though their access remains subject to local laws and additional platform-level restrictions.


This article was written by Tanya Chepkova at www.financemagnates.com.

title: Palo Alto Posts Q1 Double Beat, Announces Applied Compute Acquisition
description:
Palo Alto Networks Inc (NASDAQ:PANW) posted financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 after the closing bell on Wednesday. Here’s a rundown of the cybersecurity company’s report.
Palo Alto Networks stock is trending today. What’s behind the PANW action?
Palo Alto Q1 Earnings Highlights
Palo Alto reported first-quarter revenue of $3.45 billion, beating analyst estimates of $3.31 billion. The company reported adjusted earnings of $1.05 per share for the quarter, beating estimates of 97 cents per share, according to Benzinga Pro.
Total revenue was up 39% year-over-year, and remaining performance obligations grew 35% year-over-year to $21 billion. The company said next-generation security annual recurring revenue increased 66% year-over-year to $9.73 billion.
Palo Alto generated $1.9 billion in adjusted free cash flow during the quarter and exited the period with approximately $2.59 billion in cash and cash equivalents.
“As AI reshapes the threat landscape, we must continually evolve to protect our customers and enable them to adopt AI securely,” said Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks.
In connection with earnings, Palo Alto announced it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Applied Compute, a platform for post-training and inference of open-weight AI models. The all-stock transaction is valued at $4.5 billion and is expected to close in the company’s fiscal third quarter.
What’s Next For Palo Alto?
Palo Alto expects second-quarter revenue to be in the range of $3.53 billion to $3.55 billion versus estimates of $3.42 billion. The company anticipates second-quarter adjusted earnings between $1.01 and $1.03 per share versus estimates of $1.01 per share.
Palo Alto also raised its fiscal 2027 guidance. The company now expects full-year revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion versus estimates of $14.16 billion, and adjusted earnings of $4.26 to $4.30 per share versus estimates of $4.18 per share.
Palo Alto management will further discuss the quarter on an earnings call at 4:30 p.m. ET. A link to the call has been provided below.
PANW Stock Rises After Earnings
PANW Price Action: Palo Alto shares were up 8.11% in after-hours trading at $367.50 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro.

title: Alzheimer’s blood marker could predict cognitive decline risks, says Mayo Clinic
description: A Mayo Clinic study finds a p-tau217 blood test may predict cognitive decline risk within five to 10 years, offering a less invasive option than PET scans.
fullContent:
A blood test that detects a protein linked to Alzheimer’s disease could help predict whether older adults will develop cognitive decline within five to 10 years, according to a new Mayo Clinic study published in JAMA Neurology.

The study looked at levels of phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) in 2,178 cognitively unimpaired adults, ranging in age from 60 to 90. It also considered age, gender and whether participants carried the APOE ε4 genetic variant, which is associated with Alzheimer’s risk.

The participants – drawn from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging and the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative – underwent blood biomarker testing, genetic testing and multiple cognitive assessments.

ALZHEIMER'S WARNING SIGNS COULD EMERGE YEARS BEFORE MEMORY LOSS, STUDY FINDS

While APOE ε4 had a modest association with risk after accounting for p-tau217, older age was associated with greater risk, according to the researchers.

For example, at the same elevated p-tau217 level, a 65-year-old faced a 6% estimated five-year risk of mild cognitive impairment, compared to a 37% risk for an 85-year-old.

Alzheimer’s disease is marked by plaques and tangles that accumulate in the brain, noted senior author Clifford Jack Jr., M.D., a Mayo Clinic neuroradiologist.

"The test tells you, just by taking a blood sample, whether someone has that pathology in the brain," he told Fox News Digital, adding that higher levels of the pathology are associated with a greater risk of progressing from normal cognition to impairment.

10 HEALTH CONDITIONS MAY BE LINKED TO ALZHEIMER'S YEARS BEFORE DIAGNOSIS

Detecting p-tau217 in blood may be "less invasive and potentially more scalable" than using PET scans to measure amyloid burden, a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease that is associated with future cognitive impairment.

"The goal is to provide a personalized estimate of the risk of developing cognitive impairment that is more meaningful than simply reporting whether a blood test is positive or negative for amyloid pathology," said first author Alicia Algeciras-Schimnich, Ph.D., a Mayo Clinic laboratory medicine and pathology researcher, in a news release.

If investigational treatments are found to be effective at preventing or delaying cognitive decline, this blood test could take on greater significance, according to the researchers.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"If preventive treatments become available, this kind of information could help patients and clinicians have more informed conversations about the potential benefits and risks of treatment," Jack noted.

The risk estimates were developed in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging, which is drawn from a specific geographical area.

"The older population in southeast Minnesota is not representative of the entire United States," Jack said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

While the study’s methods could be applied in other populations, the researcher said the findings need to be replicated outside the region.

The risk prediction model is not yet ready for routine screening of people without cognitive symptoms, according to the research team.

"There is no treatment that’s been approved for people who are [asymptomatic] but have the disease in the brain," Jack told Fox News Digital. "Therefore, there’s no reason to do the test. … The results of the test would not change your medical management at all since there’s no treatment available."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

That could change if preventive treatments are approved, he added.

The study does not establish that routine blood testing prevents dementia or improves clinical outcomes.

"Many elderly people who have the pathology in the brain at lower levels will never develop symptoms in their lifetime," Jack added, noting that some people with Alzheimer’s-related pathology may also die of another cause before developing cognitive impairment.

title: US races to build bunkers across Middle East as Iranian strikes threaten American troops
description: The U.S. Army is hiring contractors to build 17 reinforced concrete bunkers in Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon amid Iranian missile and drone attacks.
fullContent:
The U.S. Army is racing to hire contractors to build 17 reinforced concrete bunkers in Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon to protect American and coalition troops from deadly missile and drone attacks, according to a government procurement notice posted Friday.

The move comes amid escalating violence in the Middle East, where Iranian attacks on U.S. military installations have killed at least 23 American service members since war broke out in late February.

On Tuesday, Iran also claimed responsibility for another strike on a U.S. military base in Bahrain, its third attack there in five days.

BAHRAIN INTERCEPTS IRANIAN DRONES TARGETING US RADAR AFTER 2-MONTH LULL IN GULF STRIKES

Kuwaiti air defenses also intercepted incoming drones as Israeli forces launched new strikes in eastern and southern Lebanon.

The Army plans to build 10 bunkers in Israel, five in Saudi Arabia and two in Lebanon, replacing makeshift shelters made from shipping containers.

"Due to elevated regional force protection conditions, there is an urgent, high-priority requirement to replace nonstandard personnel protection shelters (e.g., converted shipping containers) and provide standardized, precast, reinforced concrete Indirect Fire bunkers," the Army said in the notice.

"The objective is to safeguard U.S. and coalition service members operating in potentially hostile environments across multiple countries in [U.S. Central Command] Area of Responsibility," the notice added.

PENTAGON JUMPS FROM $225M TO $55B ON DRONES AS CHEAP ATTACKS OVERWHELM US DEFENSES

The effort also follows a series of Iranian missile and drone attacks on U.S. bases across the Persian Gulf.

A March drone strike on a U.S. Army command post at Kuwait's Port of Shuaiba killed six American service members, with reports saying the facility lacked adequate protection against aerial attacks.

President Donald Trump said Nov. 16 that defensive measures had been effective across the region.

"Iran has fired between 8,000-9,000 One-way Attack Drones. Only 2 of them got through, resulting in U.S. fatalities, both on the first day, hitting Kuwait and Saudi Arabia. Likewise, Iran has fired about 2,000 Ballistic Missiles. Only 1 out of the 2,0000 got through, and caused U.S. fatalities (Jordan)," he wrote on Truth Social.

US CARRIES OUT SELF-DEFENSE STRIKE ON IRGC MISSILE LAUNCH SITE ON QESHM ISLAND

"Translation: 99.99% of Iranian missiles and drones have been shot down or, in any event, not caused U.S. deaths. [U.S. Central Command] defensive measures have been historically effective. No one in the World has the ability to do so well. All of this being left out of the 60 Minutes ‘report,’" he added.

The 17 bunkers will be built at five military installations: one in Israel and two each in Saudi Arabia and Lebanon, the notice said.

The Army is withholding the sites' locations for security reasons, saying names and coordinates will be provided only to eligible contractors once the formal solicitation is issued.

Each bunker will have three precast, reinforced concrete sections, steel entrance doors shielded by concrete barriers and sandbag-reinforced exterior walls.

Each roof will be covered with at least 18 inches of layered sandbags to protect against incoming fire.

US PULLS PERSONNEL FROM SAUDI ARABIA AS KINGDOM COMES UNDER HOUTHI FIRE

Contractors will have 45 days to finish construction after receiving a task order, while bidders will have just three days to submit quotes.

"Due to extreme operational urgency (soldiers currently at risk using non-standard containerized shelters), the subsequent solicitation is anticipated to have an expedited 3-day quote turnaround window," the Army said.

The Army is looking for construction and engineering firms that can deploy to Israel, Saudi Arabia and Lebanon.

Contractors must respond by Nov. 25, and specify whether they can work in all three countries or only certain locations.

The Army is looking for "qualified, capable, and licensed construction and engineering firms with immediate cross-border and local mobilization capabilities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the State of Israel, and the Republic of Lebanon," the notice said.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Pentagon for comment.

title: Anthropic Prices IPO at $83: What a $1.5 Trillion Valuation Means for ANT Buyers
description:
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share and sold more stock than planned. See what a $1.5 trillion valuation means for ANT buyers.
The post Anthropic Prices IPO at $83: What a $1.5 Trillion Valuation Means for ANT Buyers appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Anthropic priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 a share, above its $70 to $78 range, Bloomberg reported. It also sold more shares than planned, and with a private share sale the deal tops SpaceX’s record IPO.

Retail investors requested close to $100 billion of the stock, which will trade as ANT, CNBC reported. They will pay 6% more than the original ceiling.

What an $83 Price Means for ANT Buyers

Underwriters set aside up to 20% of shares for individual investors, Reuters reported. A typical IPO reserves 5% to 10%.

At $78, Anthropic was valued near $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis, which counts stock options and restricted shares. At $83, that rises to about $1.5 trillion, by BeInCrypto’s calculation, before counting the extra shares sold.

Excluding options and restricted shares, the $78 figure falls closer to $1 trillion.

At $1.5 trillion, buyers pay about 18 times Anthropic’s $81 billion annual revenue pace. That is about 43 times its $35 billion in sales over the past 12 months, by BeInCrypto’s calculation.

Rival OpenAI’s last private valuation was $1.25 trillion, TNW reported.

BeInCrypto flagged the premium early. On Monday, it reported that traders on Hyperliquid, a crypto trading platform, had already priced Anthropic shares at a premium.

SpaceX, the last record IPO, rose 19% on its first day of trading in June.

Revenue rose 13 times to $33.2 billion in the nine months to September. Still, Anthropic booked a $104 billion net loss in that period, per its amended filing.

How Anthropic’s Raise Tops SpaceX

At $83, the original 825 million shares alone raise about $68.5 billion, by BeInCrypto’s calculation. Anthropic sold more than that after upsizing the deal, Bloomberg reported.

Seven partners, including Google and Nvidia, will also buy $26 billion of non-voting stock at the final price, per Fortune. That lifts the total to at least $94.5 billion, before the extra shares.

SpaceX’s June listing raised $85.7 billion, according to TNW. That total includes extra shares sold to underwriters, while Anthropic’s counts the private sale.

Orders reached nearly $500 billion before the move, CNBC reported. None are binding.

Anthropic Priced High Into a Shaky Market

Anthropic priced higher after AI-linked stocks led a $2.2 trillion global selloff on Monday.

Shares begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

The post Anthropic Prices IPO at $83: What a $1.5 Trillion Valuation Means for ANT Buyers appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Kim Jong Un's nuclear buildup sparks 'serious concern' ahead of Trump-Xi-Putin summit
description: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi warned Kim Jong Un's North Korean uranium enrichment expansion at Yongbyon is complete, calling it a serious concern.
fullContent:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is accelerating his nuclear program, expanding a uranium enrichment facility that can produce plutonium for nuclear weapons, the United Nations' nuclear watchdog warned Wednesday, calling Pyongyang's growing program a "cause for serious concern."

International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Director General Rafael Grossi said the latest construction at the Yongbyon nuclear complex began in mid-September and was externally complete by late October, raising fresh alarms about North Korea's production of weapons-grade nuclear material.

"The ongoing expansion of the DPRK's uranium enrichment programme remains a cause for serious concern," Grossi said in remarks to the IAEA's board of governors in Vienna, referring to North Korea by its official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

TRUMP ARRIVES IN PHILIPPINES AHEAD OF XI JINPING SUMMIT IN CHINA AFTER GOP MIDTERM LOSSES

The warning came as President Donald Trump prepared to meet President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented three-way summit expected to address nuclear arms negotiations and other global security concerns.

Trump had also floated the possibility of meeting Kim during his trip to China, potentially opening another diplomatic channel with the North Korean dictator as Pyongyang continues to reject demands that it abandon its nuclear arsenal.

TRUMP CANNOT DETER XI AND PUTIN’S NUCLEAR GOALS WITH A STRATEGY DESIGNED FOR JUST ONE

As he departed the White House on Monday, Trump told reporters that denuclearization would be among the issues discussed with world leaders.

"We're going to talk about denuclearization – tough subject, because it's very hard for any of us to say we'll get rid of our nukes," Trump said.

The president also raised the possibility of Kim joining the diplomatic discussions, although no meeting with the North Korean leader has been confirmed.

"He may come. I don't know. That's up to President Xi," Trump told reporters. Trump also said he believed there was an opportunity for progress.

"So that'll be good. We have a chance to accomplish a lot," he added.

TRUMP TEASES POTENTIAL KIM JONG UN MEETING LATER THIS YEAR

The possibility of a meeting gained attention after Russia's Interfax news agency quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying Putin could meet Kim if the North Korean leader traveled to China for the summit, according to Reuters.

Trump said Tuesday that Kim would like to meet with him, adding, "We'll see what happens."

North Korea has repeatedly rejected calls to dismantle its nuclear weapons program, even as international monitors report continued construction and activity at key nuclear facilities.

Grossi said the IAEA had previously reported ongoing enrichment operations at Yongbyon and Kangson, construction of an additional enrichment facility at Yongbyon and indications of further expansion of North Korea's production of weapons-grade nuclear material.

"Since mid-September 2026, a further extension to the original Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction with the new extension externally complete by late-October 2026," Grossi said.

The agency also observed indications that Yongbyon's 5-megawatt reactor, which can produce plutonium for nuclear weapons, likely will continue to operate in its seventh irradiation cycle.

A separate light-water reactor at the complex resumed operations at the end of April following a shutdown, according to the agency.

NORTH KOREA MISSILE COULD PUT GUAM IN RANGE AS KIM REBUFFS TRUMP OUTREACH: EXPERT

"The continuation and further development of the DPRK's nuclear programme are clear violations of relevant UN Security Council resolutions and are deeply regrettable," Grossi said.

The IAEA has not had inspectors inside North Korea since 2009, when Pyongyang expelled them.

The agency now relies primarily on satellite imagery and other publicly available information to monitor nuclear developments, limiting its ability to independently verify activity inside the facilities.

North Korea carried out its first nuclear weapons test in 2006 and five additional tests through 2017, prompting successive rounds of U.N. Security Council sanctions targeting its nuclear and ballistic missile programs.

In September, IAEA member states also expressed "growing concern" over increased nuclear activity in North Korea, while Kim's sister, Kim Yo Jong, dismissed the pressure and said North Korea's status as a nuclear-armed country was "absolute" while calling those who continued to seek its denuclearization "idiots."

TRUMP REVEALS EXACT NUMBER OF NORTH KOREA'S NUCLEAR WEAPONS

Kim has also indicated that future talks with Washington would depend on the United States abandoning its demand for denuclearization and instead negotiating with North Korea as a nuclear-armed state.

The two leaders met in Singapore in 2018, when they signed a broad statement committing to work toward the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.

Their second summit, in Hanoi in 2019, ended without an agreement after negotiations broke down over North Korea's nuclear facilities and demands for sanctions relief.

Trump and Kim met again in June 2019 at the Demilitarized Zone separating North and South Korea, where Trump briefly crossed into North Korean territory.

Those meetings also failed to secure a verifiable agreement to dismantle North Korea's nuclear weapons program.

title: Encrypted Account: a PIN that lives in the contract
description:
TL;DR
Encrypted Account is an ERC-4337 smart account that keeps a PIN inside the contract, encrypted under Zama’s threshold FHE. The contract itself checks the PIN and counts the guesses; no server holds either.
Every guess is counted on-chain before its result can be decrypted. The PIN cannot be brute-forced offline, and online guessing is limited to about 12 guesses in 30 days.
The key alone can only pay known addresses within set limits. A new address, a large amount or an arbitrary call needs the PIN and a delay.
A guess that the owner’s second device has not co-signed must carry an ETH bond that doubles with each wrong guess. A wrong guess leaves the bond in the account, so a thief with a stolen key pays the owner for every miss.
The escape needs no FHE. The key alone starts it, and after a delay the funds go to an address the owner chose in advance.
Research prototype on Sepolia, unaudited, MIT.
Motivation
Stolen keys remain the main way self-custody fails. Keys leak through malware, phishing and compromised devices, not only through lost seed phrases. In 2025, Chainalysis counted 158,000 personal-wallet compromises with at least 80,000 victims (The Block).
Today’s defenses move the problem rather than solve it. Co-signer services add a server or a second device to every payment, and social recovery is slow. On-chain spending limits are public, so a thief knows exactly what he can take.
A second factor that the contract checks itself would close this gap. But a knowledge factor on a public chain usually fails in one of two ways. If the data that verifies it is public (a hash, a commitment, a ZK verification key), a 6-digit PIN falls to offline brute force: 10⁶ candidates are too few, even behind a slow hash. If verification happens off-chain (a server, a TEE, an MPC committee), the rate limit lives off-chain too, with its own trust and liveness.
The idea: count first, reveal after
FHE lets the contract hold both the secret and the counter. The PIN fingerprint is stored as a ciphertext, the comparison runs on ciphertexts, and the result is an encrypted bit. The contract decides when that bit may be decrypted, so it can count every attempt before anyone sees its result.
Setup. The client derives h = first64(Argon2id(PIN, salt)) (64 MiB, t = 3; the salt binds the chain and the account) and stores Enc(h). The PIN never leaves the device.
Challenge. Opening an operation emits c = H(tag, chainId, account, opId, opHash), bound to the operation’s content.
Guess. The client sends Enc((h + c) mod 2^64) with an input proof. The account adds a provisional point to the wrong-guess score, compares under FHE and marks only the result bit as decryptable. For a transfer, a second bit gives the delay class; it is masked by the first, so a wrong guess learns nothing about the limits.
Finalize. Anyone relays the threshold network’s signed result. A correct guess removes its own point and starts the operation’s delay; a wrong one keeps the point and starts a back-off.
The contract never reveals the result of a guess it has not counted. A guess is bound to one challenge, so it is useless for any other operation.
client                               account (on-chain)                     threshold network
open(op) ──────────────────────────► emit challenge c
Enc((h + c) mod 2^64) + proof ─────► score += 1, hold the bond
                                     ok = (Enc(h) + c == guess), under FHE
                                     mark only ok decryptable ────────────► decrypt one bit
anyone: finalize(ok, signature) ───► ok: refund the point and the bond, start the delay
                                     wrong: keep both, start a back-off
execute after the delay ───────────► transfer

Design
The key alone covers small payments to known addresses; everything else needs the PIN and a delay, and an escape covers the worst case. A watchtower, an off-chain service the owner names at setup, relays the second phase of each check and alerts the owner. It can only restrict the account and read alarm bits, and it never holds funds.



Two paths. The key (K) alone can pay known recipients up to a daily per-asset limit. Anything else, such as a new recipient, a large amount, an unlimited approval or an arbitrary call, needs K, the PIN and a delay: 1 hour by default, 48 hours for large amounts and arbitrary calls.
Tighten fast, loosen slow. Anything that only tightens the rules, such as removing a known address, lowering a limit, restricting the account or switching off recovery, takes the key alone and applies at once. Loosening takes the PIN and a delay (24 to 72 hours by default).
Hidden rules. In the encrypted-policy variant, the known lists and the limits are ciphertexts, and the real cut-off is a random tripwire below the limit that nobody knows, the owner included. A K-only payment that fails any check moves to the PIN path without saying which. One above the tripwire also sets a sticky alarm that only the watchtower can read, and K-only payments stay blocked until the owner clears it with the PIN.
Rate limit. There is no wait after the first two wrong guesses, then 15 min · 4^(n−3), capped at 7 days; the score decays by one point every 7 days. A correct PIN never resets the score (an early version that did allowed 2,307 guesses in 30 days). A simulation of the contract’s exact rules gives at most 12 guesses in 30 days if the owner does nothing.
Bond. A guess made with the key alone, or by anyone through the recovery track, must carry an ETH bond from outside the account, never from its balance. It starts at 0.001 ETH and doubles with that track’s wrong-guess score: 0.002, 0.004 and so on. A correct guess gets its bond back; a wrong one leaves it in the account, so every miss adds to the owner’s balance. The owner can raise the key-track base up to 100 ETH with a PIN-verified change; the recovery track does not follow it yet (see Limitations).
Second device. Guesses co-signed by the owner’s second device (or a recovery helper) carry no bond and have their own back-off budget, so a thief with the key alone cannot lock the owner out of that path.
Escape. K alone starts it. It cancels every pending operation, closes the anonymous guessing tracks and the K-only path, and fixes the escape address. After 30 days by default, anyone can execute the sweep, but only to that address, which can only be set with its own consent signature. The escape uses no FHE, so it works even if the FHE network is down; only the second-device path, with the PIN, can cancel it.
Signatures. ERC-1271 accepts only hashes approved through a PIN-verified operation, so a permit phished with the key alone is void.
Seedless recovery. An owner who loses the key can propose a new one with the PIN alone, through the bonded recovery track. It executes after 7 days, or 30 days if the owner registered a second device that did not co-sign. The owner can stop it by starting the escape or by vetoing with K and the second device. It is on by default, and the key alone can switch it off.
Duress PIN (optional). A second PIN passes the check but sets a silent-alarm bit that only the watchtower can decrypt. The slot is always filled, with FHE randomness when no duress PIN is chosen, so nobody can tell which accounts have one. In open mode it is an alarm, not a brake: the transfer forced out of the owner still goes through.
What a thief with the key can do
A thief who steals the seed phrase but not the PIN can take little and pays for every guess.
He can pay addresses already on the known list, up to the hidden daily limit. A payment that fails a check moves to the PIN path without saying which, and one above the tripwire sets off a silent alarm.
He cannot pay his own address or move a large amount without the PIN, and a permit signed with the key alone is void.
He can guess the PIN about 12 times in 30 days, paying a doubling bond each time: about 0.65 ETH in total at the default base. Every wrong guess pays the owner and triggers an alert, and three wrong guesses on the key track restrict the account, which stops key-only payments.
The owner answers with the escape. Once it starts, guessing and key-only payments stop, and after the delay the funds land at the escape address.
With human-chosen 6-digit PINs and no blocklist, 12 throttled guesses succeed about 7% of the time, and 4 guesses (an escape within the first hour) about 2.6% (Markert et al., IEEE S&P 2020). Below 10 guesses the curve is interpolated linearly, so the second figure is optimistic. With a random PIN from the app’s generator, 12 guesses succeed about 0.0015% of the time. The app offers a random PIN, rejects only a short list of the most common PINs and warns about other guessable ones.
A thief who does find the PIN still waits out the PIN-path delay, and the owner’s escape cancels the pending operation.
What you have to trust
Every second factor moves trust somewhere; the question is where.
Second factor
Checked by
You must trust




Co-signer service (SMS, email or app code)
A company’s server
Its honesty and uptime; it sees every payment


TEE enclave
A secure chip run by an operator
The chip vendor, side channels and the operator’s uptime


MPC key shares
A group of share holders
That enough of them never collude, and their uptime


Passkey or fingerprint
The phone’s secure chip
The phone and its vendor; whoever unlocks the phone can sign


Email recovery
The email provider
The provider’s signing keys and the inbox


Multisig (k of n)
The chain
That k keys are never taken together; the rules are public


Encrypted Account
The contract, under FHE
Zama’s threshold network and its governance




In the first five rows, a party off-chain decides whether the second factor is right. A multisig decides on-chain but needs several keys for every payment and shows its rules to a thief. The FHE PIN decides on-chain too, with the counter and the rules hidden, so no server holds the PIN or decides on the limit. The trust that remains sits in a threshold network rather than one operator, and the escape does not depend even on that.
With a multisig or a passkey. The designs compose:
An Encrypted Account can be one signer of a multisig. Its ERC-1271 signature exists only for hashes approved with the PIN and a delay, so a stolen key of that signer cannot co-sign.
A multisig can be the account’s key: it calls the account directly, so key-only payments need its quorum and everything else still needs the PIN.
The escape address can be a cold multisig, which consents to its role with an ERC-1271 signature.
The second device can be a passkey behind an ERC-1271 wrapper, so a fingerprint co-signs the guesses that need no bond.
We have not tested these combinations yet.
Status and cost
Encrypted Account is a research prototype: unaudited, testnet only, MIT. Measured on Sepolia with the public testnet relayer and KMS:
What
Result




PIN flow, end to end (desktop client, N = 30)
p50 24.4 s, p95 47.7 s


Input proof on a mid-range phone
p95 13.65 s


PIN-verified transfer (request, guess, finalize, execute)
≈ 2.7M gas

fullContent:
TL;DR

  • Encrypted Account is an ERC-4337 smart account that keeps a PIN inside the contract, encrypted under Zama’s threshold FHE. The contract itself checks the PIN and counts the guesses; no server holds either.
  • Every guess is counted on-chain before its result can be decrypted. The PIN cannot be brute-forced offline, and online guessing is limited to about 12 guesses in 30 days.
  • The key alone can only pay known addresses within set limits. A new address, a large amount or an arbitrary call needs the PIN and a delay.
  • A guess that the owner’s second device has not co-signed must carry an ETH bond that doubles with each wrong guess. A wrong guess leaves the bond in the account, so a thief with a stolen key pays the owner for every miss.
  • The escape needs no FHE. The key alone starts it, and after a delay the funds go to an address the owner chose in advance.
  • Research prototype on Sepolia, unaudited, MIT.

Motivation

Stolen keys remain the main way self-custody fails. Keys leak through malware, phishing and compromised devices, not only through lost seed phrases. In 2025, Chainalysis counted 158,000 personal-wallet compromises with at least 80,000 victims (The Block).

Today’s defenses move the problem rather than solve it. Co-signer services add a server or a second device to every payment, and social recovery is slow. On-chain spending limits are public, so a thief knows exactly what he can take.

A second factor that the contract checks itself would close this gap. But a knowledge factor on a public chain usually fails in one of two ways. If the data that verifies it is public (a hash, a commitment, a ZK verification key), a 6-digit PIN falls to offline brute force: 10⁶ candidates are too few, even behind a slow hash. If verification happens off-chain (a server, a TEE, an MPC committee), the rate limit lives off-chain too, with its own trust and liveness.

The idea: count first, reveal after

FHE lets the contract hold both the secret and the counter. The PIN fingerprint is stored as a ciphertext, the comparison runs on ciphertexts, and the result is an encrypted bit. The contract decides when that bit may be decrypted, so it can count every attempt before anyone sees its result.

  1. Setup. The client derives h = first64(Argon2id(PIN, salt)) (64 MiB, t = 3; the salt binds the chain and the account) and stores Enc(h). The PIN never leaves the device.
  2. Challenge. Opening an operation emits c = H(tag, chainId, account, opId, opHash), bound to the operation’s content.
  3. Guess. The client sends Enc((h + c) mod 2^64) with an input proof. The account adds a provisional point to the wrong-guess score, compares under FHE and marks only the result bit as decryptable. For a transfer, a second bit gives the delay class; it is masked by the first, so a wrong guess learns nothing about the limits.
  4. Finalize. Anyone relays the threshold network’s signed result. A correct guess removes its own point and starts the operation’s delay; a wrong one keeps the point and starts a back-off.

The contract never reveals the result of a guess it has not counted. A guess is bound to one challenge, so it is useless for any other operation.

client                               account (on-chain)                     threshold network
open(op) ──────────────────────────► emit challenge c
Enc((h + c) mod 2^64) + proof ─────► score += 1, hold the bond
                                     ok = (Enc(h) + c == guess), under FHE
                                     mark only ok decryptable ────────────► decrypt one bit
anyone: finalize(ok, signature) ───► ok: refund the point and the bond, start the delay
                                     wrong: keep both, start a back-off
execute after the delay ───────────► transfer

Design

The key alone covers small payments to known addresses; everything else needs the PIN and a delay, and an escape covers the worst case. A watchtower, an off-chain service the owner names at setup, relays the second phase of each check and alerts the owner. It can only restrict the account and read alarm bits, and it never holds funds.

  • Two paths. The key (K) alone can pay known recipients up to a daily per-asset limit. Anything else, such as a new recipient, a large amount, an unlimited approval or an arbitrary call, needs K, the PIN and a delay: 1 hour by default, 48 hours for large amounts and arbitrary calls.
  • Tighten fast, loosen slow. Anything that only tightens the rules, such as removing a known address, lowering a limit, restricting the account or switching off recovery, takes the key alone and applies at once. Loosening takes the PIN and a delay (24 to 72 hours by default).
  • Hidden rules. In the encrypted-policy variant, the known lists and the limits are ciphertexts, and the real cut-off is a random tripwire below the limit that nobody knows, the owner included. A K-only payment that fails any check moves to the PIN path without saying which. One above the tripwire also sets a sticky alarm that only the watchtower can read, and K-only payments stay blocked until the owner clears it with the PIN.
  • Rate limit. There is no wait after the first two wrong guesses, then 15 min · 4^(n−3), capped at 7 days; the score decays by one point every 7 days. A correct PIN never resets the score (an early version that did allowed 2,307 guesses in 30 days). A simulation of the contract’s exact rules gives at most 12 guesses in 30 days if the owner does nothing.
  • Bond. A guess made with the key alone, or by anyone through the recovery track, must carry an ETH bond from outside the account, never from its balance. It starts at 0.001 ETH and doubles with that track’s wrong-guess score: 0.002, 0.004 and so on. A correct guess gets its bond back; a wrong one leaves it in the account, so every miss adds to the owner’s balance. The owner can raise the key-track base up to 100 ETH with a PIN-verified change; the recovery track does not follow it yet (see Limitations).
  • Second device. Guesses co-signed by the owner’s second device (or a recovery helper) carry no bond and have their own back-off budget, so a thief with the key alone cannot lock the owner out of that path.
  • Escape. K alone starts it. It cancels every pending operation, closes the anonymous guessing tracks and the K-only path, and fixes the escape address. After 30 days by default, anyone can execute the sweep, but only to that address, which can only be set with its own consent signature. The escape uses no FHE, so it works even if the FHE network is down; only the second-device path, with the PIN, can cancel it.
  • Signatures. ERC-1271 accepts only hashes approved through a PIN-verified operation, so a permit phished with the key alone is void.
  • Seedless recovery. An owner who loses the key can propose a new one with the PIN alone, through the bonded recovery track. It executes after 7 days, or 30 days if the owner registered a second device that did not co-sign. The owner can stop it by starting the escape or by vetoing with K and the second device. It is on by default, and the key alone can switch it off.
  • Duress PIN (optional). A second PIN passes the check but sets a silent-alarm bit that only the watchtower can decrypt. The slot is always filled, with FHE randomness when no duress PIN is chosen, so nobody can tell which accounts have one. In open mode it is an alarm, not a brake: the transfer forced out of the owner still goes through.

What a thief with the key can do

A thief who steals the seed phrase but not the PIN can take little and pays for every guess.

  • He can pay addresses already on the known list, up to the hidden daily limit. A payment that fails a check moves to the PIN path without saying which, and one above the tripwire sets off a silent alarm.
  • He cannot pay his own address or move a large amount without the PIN, and a permit signed with the key alone is void.
  • He can guess the PIN about 12 times in 30 days, paying a doubling bond each time: about 0.65 ETH in total at the default base. Every wrong guess pays the owner and triggers an alert, and three wrong guesses on the key track restrict the account, which stops key-only payments.
  • The owner answers with the escape. Once it starts, guessing and key-only payments stop, and after the delay the funds land at the escape address.

With human-chosen 6-digit PINs and no blocklist, 12 throttled guesses succeed about 7% of the time, and 4 guesses (an escape within the first hour) about 2.6% (Markert et al., IEEE S&P 2020). Below 10 guesses the curve is interpolated linearly, so the second figure is optimistic. With a random PIN from the app’s generator, 12 guesses succeed about 0.0015% of the time. The app offers a random PIN, rejects only a short list of the most common PINs and warns about other guessable ones.

A thief who does find the PIN still waits out the PIN-path delay, and the owner’s escape cancels the pending operation.

What you have to trust

Every second factor moves trust somewhere; the question is where.

Second factor Checked by You must trust
Co-signer service (SMS, email or app code) A company’s server Its honesty and uptime; it sees every payment
TEE enclave A secure chip run by an operator The chip vendor, side channels and the operator’s uptime
MPC key shares A group of share holders That enough of them never collude, and their uptime
Passkey or fingerprint The phone’s secure chip The phone and its vendor; whoever unlocks the phone can sign
Email recovery The email provider The provider’s signing keys and the inbox
Multisig (k of n) The chain That k keys are never taken together; the rules are public
Encrypted Account The contract, under FHE Zama’s threshold network and its governance

In the first five rows, a party off-chain decides whether the second factor is right. A multisig decides on-chain but needs several keys for every payment and shows its rules to a thief. The FHE PIN decides on-chain too, with the counter and the rules hidden, so no server holds the PIN or decides on the limit. The trust that remains sits in a threshold network rather than one operator, and the escape does not depend even on that.

With a multisig or a passkey. The designs compose:

  • An Encrypted Account can be one signer of a multisig. Its ERC-1271 signature exists only for hashes approved with the PIN and a delay, so a stolen key of that signer cannot co-sign.
  • A multisig can be the account’s key: it calls the account directly, so key-only payments need its quorum and everything else still needs the PIN.
  • The escape address can be a cold multisig, which consents to its role with an ERC-1271 signature.
  • The second device can be a passkey behind an ERC-1271 wrapper, so a fingerprint co-signs the guesses that need no bond.

We have not tested these combinations yet.

Status and cost

Encrypted Account is a research prototype: unaudited, testnet only, MIT. Measured on Sepolia with the public testnet relayer and KMS:

What Result
PIN flow, end to end (desktop client, N = 30) p50 24.4 s, p95 47.7 s
Input proof on a mid-range phone p95 13.65 s
PIN-verified transfer (request, guess, finalize, execute) ≈ 2.7M gas
Key-only transfer, encrypted lists and limit ≈ 1.76M gas
Key-only transfer, public lists and limit ≈ 60k gas

Sepolia already prices a new storage slot about five times higher than mainnet does today, and FHE state is storage-heavy. On today’s mainnet schedule, the first two transfers model to about 1.8M and 1.1M gas. The public-list variant gives up the hidden lists, limit and tripwire for a key-only transfer about 30 times cheaper.

The repository also contains a hidden will (heirs with encrypted shares), which this post leaves out.

Limitations and open questions

Like any FHE application, the design inherits the trust assumptions of Zama’s network, and a few edges are still open.

  • Trust in Zama. Confidentiality relies on Zama’s threshold KMS, which fails if 5 of its 13 nodes collude. Integrity relies on an honest majority of coprocessors, and both rely on contracts that Zama’s governance can upgrade.
  • A leaked fingerprint. If the network leaks h, the PIN check is bypassed, and about 10⁶ Argon2id runs recover the PIN itself: roughly two days on one core, about an hour on a large server. With seedless recovery on, that leak plus 7 days without a reaction from the owner (30 with a registered second device) is enough to take over an account. Ciphertexts stay on-chain, so a key that leaks later opens today’s fingerprints too.
  • A side door for the bond. The recovery track still prices guesses from 0.001 ETH, whatever base the owner set for the key track, and the two tracks share one budget. Until both follow the owner’s base, a raised base can be sidestepped there.
  • Griefing. Through the same shared budget, a stranger can push the owner’s PIN back-off to 7 days for about 0.26 ETH in bonds, which stay in the account. Owners with a second device keep their own path, and key-only payments and the escape still work.
  • Visibility and devices. In open mode, balances, amounts and recipients are public; only the rules are encrypted. A private mode with ERC-7984 tokens is in progress. If the key and the PIN are entered in the same browser, a compromised front end gets both.

Open questions

  1. In FHEVM, every persistent permission on a ciphertext is a new storage slot. As state creation gets more expensive, which patterns should apps use: transient or persistent permissions, and reusable records instead of per-operation ones?
  2. Should seedless recovery be on by default, and with what delay and bond?
  3. Is a standard worth it, for example an ERC-7579 module with a PIN-gated operation lifecycle and escape semantics?

Feedback is welcome, especially on the threat model, the rate-limit rules and the bond.

title: Dan Dakich says Dabo Swinney is done at Clemson: 'No shot he wins (another) national championship'
description: Dan Dakich says Dabo Swinney will never win another national championship, claiming the Clemson Tigers lost their momentum four or five years ago.
fullContent:

Yes, bombard me with your "Groundhog's Day" memes all you want, but this cat may have finally run out of lives as the Clemson faithful may have also run out of patience.

RANKING WHICH POWER 4 COLLEGE FOOTBALL HEAD COACHING JOB IS MOST LIKELY TO COME OPEN NEXT

CFP & ESPN INDIANA SLANDER CONTINUES, DAN DAKICH REACTS TO LATEST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RANKINGS - LISTEN NOW

THERE'S A DIFFERENCE BETWEEN COACHES WHO 'CAN'T' WIN A NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP AND COACHES WHO 'HAVEN'T'

TRANSFER PORTAL, NOT NIL, REASON FOR PARITY, CLAIMS COLLEGE FOOTBALL EXPERT BROOKS AUSTIN

The time to course correct may have already passed, though, as Dakich points out.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

title: Mullin defends TSA shoes-on policy after congressman calls classified briefing ‘very concerning’
description: Markwayne Mullin defended the TSA shoe removal policy at a House Homeland Security hearing, telling Rep. Eli Crane the change never put anyone at risk.
fullContent:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended letting travelers keep their shoes on at airport checkpoints Wednesday after an Arizona congressman pressed him on why the TSA policy remains in place despite a classified watchdog review.

"We have never put anyone at risk at all," Mullin told Rep. Eli Crane, R-Ariz., at a House Homeland Security Committee hearing.

Mullin said the department evaluates screening technology daily and that he had personally met with DHS Inspector General Joseph Cuffari in a secure facility.

"In fact, we addressed three of the four concerns," Mullin said. He said the fourth, in his view, had nothing to do with security.

TLAIB MOVES TO BLOCK ICE AIRPORT ARRESTS, SAYS TSA HELPING TARGET IMMIGRANTS

Mullin gave no specifics about what DHS had done to address the three concerns or what the fourth involved.

Crane said he had received a classified briefing from the inspector general and called it "very concerning." He asked Mullin to discuss the matter privately.

The exchange put renewed scrutiny on a July 2025 decision by then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem to end routine shoe removal at TSA checkpoints nationwide.

Noem said at the time that advances in screening technology would allow the agency to speed up lines while maintaining security. TSA officers could still ask travelers to remove their shoes for additional screening.

Within weeks of the change, the inspector general sent DHS and TSA leaders a formal warning about a screening weakness, according to questions entered into the Senate record in July.

WATCH: DEM SCOLDS HOMELAND SECURITY CHIEF TO ‘CALM DOWN’ AFTER HEARING DERAILS OVER ALLEGED ‘PATTERN’

The watchdog issued its final classified report on Nov. 1, 2025. In a March memo reviewed by CBS News, Cuffari said his office was still waiting for the agencies’ formal response after the 90-day deadline had passed.

The Senate record also shows that Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., asked TSA in April to reverse the policy until the screening weakness was addressed. In a May response cited by Cantwell, then-acting TSA Administrator Ha Nguyen McNeill said "current intelligence and risk assessments indicate no direct, credible threats related to shoes."

Mullin’s testimony Wednesday left open whether the inspector general had signed off on the steps DHS says it took.

title: Hillary Clinton dismisses Democratic leadership battle as a 'performance' as Schumer faces progressive revolt
description: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton called Sen. Chris Van Hollen's challenge to Sen. Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader a "performance."
fullContent:
Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton dismissed the leadership challenge mounted by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., against Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for Senate majority leader when Democrats take control in January as a "performance."

During Clinton and co-host Kara Swisher's podcast, "High Stakes," Wednesday, Swisher asked the former secretary of state what she thought of Van Hollen's leadership challenge to Schumer. Clinton argued Democrats were elected because voters wanted changes in their own lives, not necessarily a change in Senate or House leadership.

"So, this leadership battle, to me, is kind of performance, in a way," Clinton said. "Because if you think that the majority leader of the Senate is going to replace the voices of people like James Talarico or Abdul El-Sayed or Annie Andrews, you don't know what is going to happen in the Senate.

"The majority leader will work to get legislation up, and he'll say, 'OK, Abdul, you want to put in Medicare-for-all, and Adam Hamilton, that's not your preferred approach. You work with the legislative team here to come up with your, and let's figure out how we're going to get something passed.'"

DEMOCRATS TURN ON SCHUMER AFTER HISTORIC ELECTION WINS AS POTENTIAL CHALLENGER EMERGES

Van Hollen announced Nov. 12 that he would challenge Schumer, citing the midterm election results as a call for change.

Earlier in the discussion, Clinton said the Senate leadership election should be an open process but argued that the majority leader wasn't really the "messenger."

"I think anybody has a right to challenge the leadership of their party," she said. "I mean, it's — it should be an open process. And you know, I know Chris and have worked with him, but at this point, from my perspective, the majority leader is not the messenger. How many times did you see John Thune on television defending or espousing a message?

"Their job is different," Clinton continued. "Their job is to push the committees, to mark up legislation, get it on the floor, get it passed, get it to the House, get it to the White House.

"I want somebody who knows the ins and outs of the Senate," she said. "And just because you've been in the Senate doesn't mean that you have the, you know, hands-on experience or the team in place to really pull those parliamentary levers."

Swisher asked, "So you think it's kind of performative?" Clinton said yes. 

Swisher also asked whether Schumer would survive the challenge from Van Hollen.

"Yeah, I do," Clinton said.

SCHUMER'S LEADERSHIP RIVAL REVEALS MAJOR SENATE RULE CHANGE HE'D PURSUE IF ELECTED

Republican strategist Liz Mair told Fox News Digital, "The primary tasks of Senate majority leader are corralling votes to advance or stop legislation and literal vote counting to ensure the priorities of a caucus are advanced and agenda items they oppose are thwarted, with a healthy spoonful of good fundraising and steering of committee dollars to win tough races, something Schumer did pretty well this cycle.

"His [Van Hollen's] campaign for leader apparently being all about supposed virtue signaling to the hard left on pet policies as opposed to his ability to perform the fundamentals of the job is why he's likely to lose this contest."

Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade as both minority and majority leader, so far has 15 senators in his camp, according to previous Fox News Digital reporting.

The longtime Democratic leader has remained confident, but quiet, about his chances of retaining his job, posting shortly after Van Hollen’s announcement last week that he welcomed "discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead. I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic leader."

Van Hollen's base of support includes Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., who caucuses with Senate Democrats; Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., and Sens.-elect Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan, both progressives whom Schumer did not initially back in their respective races.

SCHUMER FACES MUTINY FROM NEWLY ELECTED SENATE DEMS AS PARTY PREPARES TO SEIZE POWER

Van Hollen's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Fox News' Alex Miller contributed to this report.
