title: Mariners acquire All-Star third baseman from Royals in first blockbuster of MLB offseason
description: The Seattle Mariners acquired All-Star third baseman Maikel Garcia from the Kansas City Royals in the first blockbuster trade of the MLB offseason.
fullContent:
The anticipated lockout on Dec. 2 has led to baseball’s hot stove heating up early.

The Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners pulled off the sport’s biggest blockbuster of the offseason on Wednesday.

The Mariners acquired All-Star third baseman Maikel Garcia, right-handed pitcher James McArthur and minor league pitcher L.P. Langevin, while the Royals received right-handed pitcher Bryce Miller, right-handed pitcher Logan Evans and left-handed pitcher José A. Ferrer, the teams announced Wednesday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

For the Mariners, they acquired their third baseman of the future in Garcia. After signing a five-year, $57.5 million contract extension with the Royals in 2025, he is under team control through 2030 with a team option in 2031.

"It is rare to have an opportunity to acquire a player signed for the long term who fits our needs as well as Maikel does," Mariners president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto said in a statement. "His ability to impact the game with his bat, his defense and his baserunning makes us a more athletic and well-rounded team."

The 26-year-old broke out in 2025, winning a Gold Glove at third base and hitting .286 with 16 home runs and 74 RBI, making the first All-Star team of his career. He regressed offensively in 2026, hitting .268 with three home runs and 38 RBI in 82 games this season. Since becoming a full-time third baseman in 2023, he has graded out as one of the best third baseman in the sport.

For the Royals, Miller and Evans will slot into their starting rotation next season.

Miller, 28, appeared in 22 games (21 starts) and had a 4-10 record with a 4.17 ERA in 118.2 innings last season with the Mariners. His best season came in 2024, when he had a 2.94 ERA in 180.1 innings across 31 starts.

Evans, 25, didn’t pitch in 2026 after undergoing UCL surgery. He appeared in 16 games (15 starts) with the Mariners in 2025 and went 6-5 with a 4.32 ERA in 81.1 innings pitched.

The Royals are banking on Miller and Evans to slot in and be instant contributors in their rotation, as the loss of Garcia weakens an already bad lineup. In 2026, the Royals averaged 4.26 runs per game, which was 22nd in baseball.

With the owners widely expected to lock out the players at midnight on Dec. 2, expect a flurry of action before the deadline, as teams cannot sign any players or trade anyone during the lockout.

title: Fed Minutes Signal More Hikes – Why Bitcoin Should Care
description:
Summary Markets did part of the Fed’s tightening. The bigger risk is a steeper path. Yields and risk appetite hit […]
The post Fed Minutes Signal More Hikes – Why Bitcoin Should Care appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Summary

  • Markets did part of the Fed’s tightening.
  • The bigger risk is a steeper path.
  • Yields and risk appetite hit Bitcoin differently.
  • November CPI arrives a day after the vote.

The Federal Reserve published the minutes of its October 27-28 meeting at 19:00 UTC on November 18, three weeks before its next decision.

Markets did part of the Fed’s work

Officials held the target range at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase, a hawkish split behind the October pause.

The full meeting record shows how firmly hikes stayed on the table. Almost all participants judged that further action to raise the target range would likely be appropriate under their baseline outlooks, with the aim of returning inflation to 2% in a timely way.

That consensus is also why the majority could wait. Some participants said market-implied tightening for December and next year was broadly consistent with their own view of the right path, and several took that alignment as a reason why holding steady carried less risk.

When markets price hikes in advance, borrowing costs often rise before the Fed votes. A pause in October therefore did not mean easier conditions for crypto; futures and yields were already doing part of the tightening.

A couple of participants went further, saying an increase larger than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data proved unfavorable. That was a conditional view from a small group, recorded in October, not a committee plan.

Futures pricing shows how little of that December step is left to surprise. As of the evening of November 18, the CME FedWatch tool, which derives probabilities from fed funds futures, put the chance of a December hike at 100%: 90.7% for a quarter point to 4.00%-4.25% and 9.3% for a half point to 4.25%-4.50%. That 9.3% is the market’s price on the larger move a couple of officials discussed, and the figure to watch as new data arrives before the vote.

The path behind the next hike

The minutes also report the median expectation from the New York Fed trading desk’s survey of market participants: one hike in December, another in March 2027, and a cut in early 2028. Collected before the meeting, it is the clearest snapshot in the document of where investors thought rates were heading.

Under that survey path, the range would reach 4.25%-4.50% after March and stay there until early 2028. With futures treating a December hike as settled, a quarter-point move adds little new information for Bitcoin. Pressure would come from a revision to the path itself, and there are three ways it could get steeper.

Step one, bigger

A December move above 25 basis points would front-load tightening and test positions built around a quarter point.

A third hike

Another increase after March would lift the expected peak, the level that sets how much idle dollars can earn.

A later first cut

Pushing relief beyond early 2028 would extend the stretch in which interest-bearing assets compete with a coin that pays nothing.

Two routes from the rate path to Bitcoin

The first route is yield competition. Bitcoin pays no interest, so every month that Treasury bills and money-market funds pay close to the policy rate raises the return a holder gives up. This route depends mostly on the level of rates and how long it lasts, which is why the timing of the first cut weighs as heavily as December’s decision.

Leveraged traders feel a version of this through borrowing costs, though not one-for-one. Exchange margin rates follow each platform’s terms, DeFi lending rates move with pool demand, and perpetual-futures funding depends on the balance between longs and shorts rather than on the Fed’s benchmark.

The second route is risk appetite. A 2023 IMF working paper by Natasha Che, Alexander Copestake, Davide Furceri and Tammaro Terracciano found that a single common factor explains about 80% of crypto price variation, and that US tightening weakened it through investors’ willingness to take risk, the same channel that moves stocks. The authors read the result as evidence against crypto working as a hedge.

The two routes react to different news. Yield competition builds slowly with the level and duration of rates, while risk appetite responds to surprises that change how much uncertainty investors are prepared to carry. A steeper path would work through both at once. The IMF study supports the direction of that effect but gives no size for any single decision.

READ MORE:

Grayscale Reveals ‘Compelling Entry Points’ but Data Says No

The data calendar into December 9

The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes October’s personal income and outlays report, which carries the PCE price index the Fed targets, at 13:30 UTC on November 25, according to its release schedule. The Bureau of Labor Statistics follows with November’s employment report on December 4.

November’s consumer price index is due on December 10, the day after the decision, per the BLS calendar. That makes October PCE the last major inflation report before the vote, and the most direct test of the “unfavorable data” condition behind the larger-hike view.

Bitcoin’s own flows, from ETF demand to derivatives positioning, will move the price alongside those numbers, so no single print explains a move by itself. The rate question for crypto over the next three weeks is narrower: whether the data bends the path the survey described, through a bigger December step, a hike after March or a later first cut. A quarter-point hike in line with that survey would leave the picture where the October minutes found it.

title: The horrible CFP committee has united America, Sophie Cunningham gets a Maxim nod & Sam Leavitt makes it worse
description: Third Hump Day of November brings CFP rankings rage as the committee keeps Alabama at 3 despite a shaky Vandy showing, uniting a divided country.
fullContent:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Third Hump Day of November, folks ...

And everyone's mad! Come on. On a Hump Day?! Of all days. We're eight days away from Thanksgiving, the grid did NOT go down yesterday as TikTok predicted, and you're all still mad?

Ah. Never mind. I get it now. The College Football Playoff rankings came out last night. Now it all makes sense. Nothing — and I mean nothing — unites this great country like the CFP rankings. We live in such a divisive time where everything is so black or white. Red or blue. Nobody can agree on anything.

There is no more middle ground ...

Except for the CFP rankings. We all hate the committee equally, and it's beautiful. SEC, Big Ten, ACC or Big 12 — it doesn't matter. Everyone has a gripe. Everyone hates them. We all band together for five weeks in the fall, and show off our complete disdain for that committee.

See? We CAN agree on something, folks! There's still hope.

Let's roll.

Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where America unites against a horrible playoff committee that refuses to upset the state of Alabama. Amazing.

And I'm an SEC guy!

What else? I've got Sophie Cunningham getting her first Maxim cover girl nod, Sam Leavitt didn't exactly help his case yesterday after an awful weekend, and GTA fever is sweeping the nation today ... for some reason.

Seriously. Wait till you see what Deshaun Watson had to say about it! A video game.

Amazing.

OK, grab you a controller and settle in for a Hump Day 'Cap!

Maybe this is a dumb question, but ... is anyone in class today still playing video games? I'm serious. Not trying to be a jerk. I honestly want to know.

MIAMI HEAT FINALLY UNVEIL 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED JERSEYS AND SOCIAL MEDIA IS LOVING THEM

The new GTA (Grand Theft Auto) comes out at midnight, and it's been a decade(s) in the making. This is the Super Bowl for a lot of folks in this country. Seriously. Folks have been waiting years for this.

Admittedly, I don't play video games anymore. I have a job and two toddlers. Where, exactly, am I supposed to carve out the time for a video game? Have you seen the stock market lately? I couldn't afford it even if I wanted to.

My question? How old is too old to be playing a video game? Is there an age? Or is it more a "stage" you reach in life (kids, marriage, etc ...)?

I'm genuinely curious. Let me know!

Now, let's get this class started with public enemy No. 1 in America today ...

The CFP committee!

Look, I'm an SEC guy. I love the SEC. I grew up watching the SEC on CBS before the dummies over at CBS ruined it by giving all the games to ESPN. I contend that the SEC is the best conference in the world.

That being said ... I truly don't understand the committee A) keeping Alabama at No. 3, or B) keeping South Carolina in the top-25. I do not get it.

'Bama is a playoff team. Nobody is arguing that. But the Crimson Tide looked like absolute garbage against an awful Vandy team last weekend, and they just ... stayed at 3? Why? Because they "found a win" at VANDERBILT?

SAM LEAVITT WAS ASKED ABOUT FINISHING LSU’S SEASON. HIS ANSWER EXPLAINS WHY COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS LOST

Give me a break.

That's just a goofy statement to make — especially with a straight face. I don't think Indiana is very good. I've gone on record saying that, and I will continue to say it. But you can't drop the Hoosiers five spots one week when they didn't even play, and then leave Alabama at 3 the next weekend when every one of their 'impressive' wins LOST.

Can't do it.

And how about South Carolina? The 'Cocks got absolutely DOG-WALKED by a truly horrific Arkansas team, yet they're still in the top-25? Come on.

Oklahoma, by the way, also has no business in the top-25. None. I think sane Sooner fans would even agree with that.

None of it makes sense. By the way, it's only going to get worse when we double the teams next season. Again, I'm an SEC guy. But it's hard to defend the committee at this point. There is no rhyme or reason to any of it. They're shooting from the hip and hoping something sticks.

The only thing they've accomplished? Somehow uniting a divided country.

Kudos.

Now, let's check in with a team that is so bad, even that terrible committee couldn't justify putting them in the top-25 ...

LSU!

Amazing. Lordy, that was bad. Everything about those two clips was just BAD for Sam Leavitt.

I wrote on Monday about how there was no loyalty left in college football, and there isn't. Listen to Sam when he was asked about his "motivation" for playing these final two regular season games:

For everyone, whether you want to go to the NFL, come back here or transfer, whatever you put out on the field is going to give yourself the best opportunity for next year. That's kind of my talk to the whole team."

You know who that sounds like? An NFL player playing on a terrible team looking for a new job next season. That's what college football has become. Free Agency. It's all transactional now. Nowhere in there did Leavitt talk about LSU or having school pride or playing for the fans.

He wants to put together a couple good weeks of tape for his next team. That's where we are now in college football. That's what it's all about.

Unless, of course, you ask Mark T.

Let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night with an ELITE email

"You wrote an article about no loyalty in college football?!?? You are about 100 years too late. When has there ever been loyalty in college football other than the fans, er, I mean customers who blindly attach themselves to something they have zero control over managed by people who could care less about them. I didn’t read your article, just the headline, no loyalty here either since Papa Joe and the Sports Babe.

"Loyalty …… just like rehabilitated, I don’t know what that word means. I know what you think it means, but to me it’s just a made up word so guys like you can wear a suit and have a job..stamp your form Sonny and quit wasting my time."

Whoaaaaaaaaaaa Nellie! What an email! I get a lot of nasty ones, but that one earns a spot on the fridge. Claiming there has NEVER been loyalty in college football is a bit of a stretch, no?

Players back in the day had to be loyal, or they had to sit out a year if they wanted to leave. That year also counted against your eligibility.

So, yeah — there used to be loyalty. You couldn't just get up and leave whenever you wanted. You couldn't play for THREE teams in three years, like Sam Leavitt is currently doing.

Also, I don't wear a suit to work. I usually wear my Dale Jr. sweatshirt and 'Gulf of America' hat like a PATRIOT.

OK, that's it for today. Good Hump Day, everyone. One week till Thanksgiving. Get your minds right.

On the way out, here's someone else who doesn't wear a suit to work ... Sophie Cunningham!

Sophie is your newest Maxim cover girl for December.

Merry Christmas indeed.

title: Walmart Could Swing By $60.6 Billion After Earnings
description:
Earnings are back in focus on Thursday, with a tight, single-day slate that spans big-box retail, consumer staples, home furnishings, test-and-measurement hardware, fintech trading and software. With guidance often doing as much work as the headline numbers, options pricing can offer a clean read on how much volatility traders are bracing for, according to Benzinga Pro.
The marquee name on this Benzinga-selected list is Walmart, but the largest implied move is saved for the final section as the countdown runs from the calmest setup to the most volatile.
6. Walmart | Mkt Cap: $1T | Implied Move: 5.99%
Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) reports third quarter of 2027 results before the opening bell. Wall Street is looking for 64 cents in earnings per share on $187.21 billion in revenue, compared with 62 cents on $179.50 billion a year ago.
Benzinga Pro data show the options market is implying a 5.99% move, the narrowest swing in this roundup — but with Walmart’s scale, it still translates into $60.6 billion of market value at stake.
Walmart remains a bellwether for consumer demand, running more than 10,700 stores globally while pushing deeper into e-commerce and serving a massive weekly customer base. The stock carries a Buy consensus rating, and the stock is trading below the 180-day average analyst price forecast. In November, Wells Fargo reiterated its Overweight rating and raised its price forecast, while Stifel maintained a Buy rating.
Walmart has rallied in 2026, up 13.1% year-to-date and trading 6.1% above the 200-day moving average even after the 50-day moving average crossed below the 200-day in July. The shares sit about 27% above the 52-week low of $99.68.
5. Post Holdings | Mkt Cap: $3.6B | Implied Move: 7.50%
Post Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:POST) reports fourth quarter of 2026 results after the closing bell. Consensus estimates call for $1.78 in EPS on $2.00 billion in revenue, down from $2.09 on $2.25 billion in the prior-year period.
Options traders are leaning into a bigger reaction here: according to Benzinga Pro, the implied move is 7.50%, putting about $273 million of market value at stake.
Post Holdings sits across several consumer packaged food categories — from center-of-the-store brands to refrigerated, foodservice and ingredients — so investors tend to parse both pricing power and mix shifts in the quarter. The company has a Buy consensus rating, and the share price sits below the 180-day average analyst price forecast. In October, Evercore ISI Group, Barclays, and Stifel cut their price forecasts, keeping the spotlight on execution as the fiscal year closes.
Post Holdings has pulled back in 2026, down 19.4% year-to-date and trading 11.8% below the 200-day moving average. The shares sit about 32% below the 52-week high of $117.28.
4. Williams-Sonoma, Inc. | Mkt Cap: $29B | Implied Move: 7.52%
Williams-Sonoma, Inc. (NYSE:WSM) reports third quarter of 2026 results before the opening bell. The Street is modeling $2.18 in EPS on $2.00 billion in revenue, compared with $1.96 on $1.88 billion a year earlier.
Benzinga Pro data show options are pricing in a 7.52% move, with roughly $2.21 billion of market value at stake — a meaningful swing for a home-furnishings retailer where demand can hinge on consumer confidence and housing-related spending.
Williams-Sonoma operates across a retail and direct-to-consumer footprint in the home category, while also working to expand exposure to B2B, marketplace and franchise channels. The stock carries a Buy consensus rating, and the 180-day average analyst price forecast is above where the stock trades. In November, Stifel initiated coverage with a Buy rating, and Barclays reiterated its Equal-Weight rating while raising its price forecast.
Williams-Sonoma has rallied in 2026, up 33.1% year-to-date and trading 15% above the 200-day moving average. The shares sit about 51% above the 52-week low of $165.51.




3. Keysight Technologies| Mkt Cap: $48B | Implied Move: 9.34%
Keysight Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:KEYS) reports fourth quarter of 2026 results after the closing bell. Analysts expect $3.37 in EPS on $1.95 billion in revenue, up from $1.91 on $1.42 billion in the year-ago quarter.
The options market is signaling a larger potential reset: Benzinga Pro shows an implied move of 9.34%, representing about $4.53 billion of market value at stake.
Keysight Technologies sells test-and-measurement tools that help electronics OEMs and suppliers bring products to market and meet industry standards — a business that can be sensitive to capex cycles and product ramps. The stock has a Buy consensus rating, and shares trade well below the 180-day average analyst price forecast. In October, Goldman Sachs reiterated its Buy rating and raised its price forecast, a reminder that the Street is still looking for follow-through as the company closes out the fiscal year.
Keysight Technologies has rallied in 2026, up 37.7% year-to-date, but it heads into the print trading 10.1% below the 200-day moving average. The shares sit about 26% below the 52-week high of $389.93.
2. Webull | Mkt Cap: $2.6B | Implied Move: 10.06%
Webull Corp. (NASDAQ:BULL) reports third quarter of 2026 results after the closing bell. Wall Street is calling for 6 cents in EPS on $218.37 million in revenue, versus 7 cents on $156.94 million a year ago.
According to Benzinga Pro, options are pricing in a 10.06% move, with about $257 million of market value at stake — a sizable implied swing for a smaller-cap trading platform where sentiment can shift quickly around growth and engagement metrics.
Webull positions itself as a low-cost, easy-to-use digital investment platform built on global infrastructure services, putting the focus on customer activity and monetization as markets fluctuate. The stock carries a Buy consensus rating, and the stock is trading well below the 180-day average analyst price forecast. In October, Scotiabank upgraded the stock to Sector Outperform, while Rosenblatt reiterated its Buy rating and cut its price forecast.
Webull has pulled back in 2026, down 42.2% year-to-date, and it trades 27.6% below the 200-day moving average after the 50-day moving average crossed below the 200-day in November. The shares sit about 53% below the 52-week high of $10.37.
1. Intuit | Mkt Cap: $86B | Implied Move: 10.72%
Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) reports first quarter of 2027 results after the closing bell. Consensus estimates call for $2.65 in EPS on $4.31 billion in revenue, compared with $3.34 on $3.88 billion in the prior-year quarter.
Benzinga Pro data show the widest implied move in this roundup lands on Intuit at 10.72%, putting about $9.19 billion of market value at stake as traders brace for a potentially sharp post-earnings repricing.
Intuit spans consumer and small-business finance workflows — from QuickBooks and Mailchimp to TurboTax, Credit Karma and professional tax tools — which makes subscriber trends and product momentum central to the narrative. The stock carries a Buy consensus rating, and the share price sits below the 180-day average analyst price forecast. In November, Wells Fargo reiterated its Equal-Weight rating and raised its price forecast and TD Cowen reiterated its Hold rating while also raising its price forecast.
Intuit has pulled back in 2026, down 49.0% year-to-date and trading 7.8% below the 200-day moving average. The shares sit about 53% below the 52-week high of $682.27.

title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for next House speaker
description:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) speaks during a press conference in the US Capitol on September 3, in Washington, DC. - Finn Gomez/Getty Images/File
Hakeem Jeffries is now all but certain to lead the House next January, a role that will make him the first Black speaker in US history as he oversees Democrats’ largest majority in years.
Roughly two weeks after their midterms romp, House Democrats voted to back Jeffries for the top job in the new Congress, despite some on the far-left clamoring for new leadership.
A small bloc of newly elected Democratic socialists had refused to publicly commit to Jeffries ahead of the leadership election, demanding concessions like votes for Medicare for All or a ban on arms sales to Israel.
But in the end, just 11 Democrats voted against him in the secret ballot vote, according to a source familiar with the vote, all but ensuring he will win the gavel in the new Congress.
“People of this country are demanding big, dramatic and transformational change. The status quo is unacceptable. And we’re committed to delivering in a meaningful way the type of change that the American people deserve,” Jeffries told reporters after clinching the nomination.
One group of seven ultra-progressive new members declared in a statement that they voted “no” because they are still seeking commitment from Jeffries on key priorities, including votes on Medicare for All and ending “the genocide in Gaza,” they said. Signed onto the statement were Reps.-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier of New York, Adam Hamawy of New Jersey, Frederick Haynes of Texas, Melat Kiros of Colorado, Donavan McKinney of Michigan, Chris Rabb of Pennsylvania and Claire Valdez of New York.
Democratic Rep.-elect Don Leonard told CNN that he also voted against nominating Jeffries for speaker, emphasizing that he wants commitments that Jeffries will prioritize key issues like money in politics and blocking US aid to Israel.
“We’re looking for a strong commitment to end the Citizens United this Congress through a 28th Amendment, and we’re looking, looking to call a vote on US aid to Israel,” said Leonard. “Until I get confirmation on those votes he does not have my support. We’ve got until the first week of January, I’m still holding out hope.”
Asked about the defectors, Jeffries would say only: “Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other.”
Ahead of his win, Jeffries received a powerful endorsement inside the room from Rep. Jim Clyburn, a longtime ally and one of the most senior members of the Congressional Black Caucus.
“Hakeem is interested in headways and not headlines,” Clyburn declared in his signature baritone voice, according to two people in the room, delivering a speech that one described as “powerful” as the caucus formally nominated the nation’s first Black speaker.
Now, all that stands between Jeffries and the gavel is a formal vote by the full chamber on the floor on January 3 — the first act of the new Congress — which his allies, and even his detractors, expect he will easily survive.
His leadership team will include Rep. Katherine Clark, who is set to become House majority leader – the first woman to hold that job – and Rep. Pete Aguilar, who will be the first Latino in history to hold the House’s No. 3 job of whip.
Jeffries had been expected to coast through the party vote on Wednesday, because the Democrats’ majority next year is simply too large for any small bloc of lawmakers to hold sway. But people close to the New York Democrat insist that he took nothing for granted.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) speaks with reporters as he departs a press conference on Capitol Hill on November 12. (Francis Chung/POLITICO via AP Images) - Francis Chung/POLITICO/AP
Ahead of the election, he lined up face-to-face conversations with any incoming Democrats who had refused to commit — nearly all aligned with the Democratic Socialists for America. He sat down with the biggest factions of his caucus, including the centrists, New Democrat Coalition and the Blue Dog Caucus, as well as the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
Jeffries and his team have kept their private discussions closely guarded. But Democrats have noted some subtle shifts in Jeffries’ public remarks, including a significant shift on one of the left’s biggest policy demands: Medicare for All.
Jeffries announced on Friday that he backs major tenets of a universal healthcare system, specifically, lowering the eligibility age for Medicare, creating a new program that guarantees universal coverage for kids and adding hearing, dental and vision coverage to the program.
It’s a major nod to progressive priorities, mirroring Sen. Bernie Sanders’ approach to a phase-in for Medicare for All system. (Centrist Democrats, meanwhile, have pushed for a Medicare-like public option.)
This story has been updated with additional developments.

CNN’s Manu Raju and Annie Grayer contributed to this report.
For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com

title: Fed Minutes: 'Almost All' Officials See More Hikes, and AI Debt Is Now on the Radar
description:
The Federal Reserve held rates in October, but officials broadly expect more increases. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF traded slightly higher in Wednesday’s regular session.
Minutes of the Oct. 27-28 meeting, released Wednesday, show that almost all officials expect further rate increases to be appropriate. They also show AI debt moving onto the Fed’s list of financial stability risks.
The committee led by Chair Kevin Warsh kept rates at 3.75% to 4%, one meeting after hiking in September. Only Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase.
Yet the hawkish camp was larger than the vote.
“Some participants favored an increase of 25 basis points in the target range at this meeting,” the minutes said.
In Fed language, “some” is a bigger group than “a few” or “several.” In addition, a few officials who backed the hold described it as a “close call.”
A Pause With a Hawkish Message
Officials worked hard to make sure markets did not read the October hold as a retreat.
“Many participants stressed the importance of clearly relaying the message that the decision to maintain the target range did not reflect a weakening of the committee’s commitment to returning inflation to 2% in a timely manner,” the minutes said.
A few participants said they “could have supported no change in the federal funds rate provided that it was clearly understood by market participants that further tightening was likely.”
Almost All Officials See More Hikes Ahead
Almost all participants judged that further rate increases, broadly in line with the September projections, would likely be appropriate under their baseline outlook.
A couple of officials went further. They said a hike larger than 25 basis points could warrant consideration in December if incoming inflation data were unfavorable.
The data explain the urgency. Fed staff estimated that headline personal consumption expenditures inflation, the Fed’s preferred gauge, rose to 3.6% in September, while core PCE edged up to 3.1%.
AI Debt Lands on the Fed’s Radar
The minutes also flagged AI as a financial stability risk. Almost all participants discussed a scenario in which returns on AI investment disappoint investors. In addition, most observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly through “complex and opaque financing structures.”
The Next Fight Is Over Words
The minutes landed the same day Fed Governor Christopher Waller pressed his case for tighter policy.
Nick Timiraos, chief economics correspondent at The Wall Street Journal, framed the issue as bigger than one meeting.
“There’s a broader point here beyond December tactics. Imagine no dot plot, no rate projection in the SEP, maybe no press conference, and no balance-of-risks language in the statement. That’s roughly the pre-1999 Greenspan setup,” Timiraos said in a post on X.
“In that world, words can’t do the work of action, because you’ve stopped using words that way. You have to act,” Timiraos added.


There’s a broader point here beyond December tactics. Imagine no dot plot, no rate projection in the SEP, maybe no press conference, and no balance-of-risks language in the statement. That’s roughly the pre-1999 Greenspan setup.
In that world, words can’t do the work of action,…
— Nick Timiraos (@NickTimiraos) November 18, 2026





In Timiraos’ reading, Waller’s message is that if the committee puts away the communication tools it built over two decades, “a 25 followed by silence about what comes next is inadequate.”
Treasury Yields Ease Despite the Hawkish Tone
The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 5 basis points to 5.06%, while the 30-year yield dropped 5 basis points to 5.41%. The 2-year yield, the most sensitive to Fed policy, slipped 1 basis point to 4.80%.
The S&P 500 fell 0.3% to 7,321, while the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.4%.
Gold dropped 3.2% to $3,728 an ounce, and Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) fell 3.2% to $62,786.
The October vote showed two hawks. The minutes show a wider group behind them, and a December meeting where the size of the next hike may be part of the debate.

title: Losing Almost $3 Million in Less Than 2 Years: The Sad Story of This Crypto Trader
description: The trader stands to lose more if TRUMP extends its decline.
fullContent:
The cryptocurrency market is a unique arena that can make investors millionaires quickly, provided they pick the right asset and time their exit wisely.

At the same time, it can be unforgiving to those who miss the opportunity to take profits or enter just as prices peak. Here’s the painful journey of one investor who lost almost $3 million in about a year and a half.

A 92% Loss… So Far

Lookonchain revealed the case of a mysterious market participant who bought 267,272 TRUMP tokens less than two years ago for $3.19 million.

The bet did not play out as expected, with the original investment now worth just $258,000. This means the investor is now sitting on an unrealized loss of roughly $2.93 million.

Of course, the primary driver behind the unsuccessful investment (at least for now) is the steep price decline of Official Trump (TRUMP), a meme coin closely associated with US President Donald Trump.

The token started trading around his inauguration in January 2025 and initially entered the crypto sector amid a storm, with its price briefly exploding to $25 and its market cap hitting $5 billion. However, the hype quickly faded, and in the months that followed, TRUMP experienced a real meltdown that only intensified after Democrats secured a decisive victory in the midterm elections in early November.

As of this writing, the meme coin trades just below $1, representing a 96% collapse from the historic peak. Its market cap has fallen to around $270 million, meaning that TRUMP is no longer among the top 100 largest cryptocurrencies.

Previous Cases

Not taking profits at the top can be just as painful as selling too early and then watching the price skyrocket. Earlier this year, Looknchain reported a trader who bought 7.99 million PONS tokens for around $443,000 and offloaded the stash as the asset’s price headed south, taking a $308,000 loss.

What’s particularly interesting is that the valuation then reversed, exploding by over 1,000% in two weeks. This means that the trader would have made a $3 million profit if they had held the stash a bit longer.

Another crazy story dates back to 2024, when one investor made more than $3 million in less than three days after dealing with certain meme coins like SLERF.

title: Waller's Rate-Hike Warning Puts 3 TIPS ETFs' Inflation Protection to the Test
description:
Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller’s warning that policymakers may need to “shock people” with a 50-basis-point rate hike in December is putting the spotlight on inflation protection once again. TIP shares were trading slightly higher in regular trading Wednesday. For ETF investors, the question is whether Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) funds can help preserve purchasing power without exposing portfolios to excessive interest-rate risk.
Waller said Wednesday that inflation is spreading across the economy and businesses are increasingly treating price increases of around 3% as normal. He urged the Federal Open Market Committee to consider a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting or raise rates by a quarter point and signal another increase in January.
The comments highlight growing concerns that inflation could remain stubbornly above the Fed’s 2% target, even as policymakers debate the pace of further tightening.
TIPS ETFs Offer an Inflation Hedge, but There’s a Catch
That backdrop could renew interest in inflation-linked ETFs, particularly the  Vanguard Short-Term Inflation-Protected Securities ETF (NASDAQ:VTIP), the iShares 0-5 Year TIPS Bond ETF (NYSE:STIP) and the iShares TIPS Bond ETF (NYSE:TIP).
Unlike conventional Treasury bonds, TIPS adjust their principal based on changes in the Consumer Price Index (CPI). This allows investors to receive inflation-linked adjustments while retaining exposure to U.S. government debt.
However, rising inflation does not automatically translate into higher ETF returns. When the Fed raises rates, real yields can also climb, putting downward pressure on existing TIPS prices. Funds with longer-duration exposure are generally more sensitive to these movements.
The 2022 rate-hiking cycle offers a telling example. Despite CPI rising 6.5% in the 12 months through December 2022, the Morningstar US TIPS Index declined approximately 12% that year, according to Morningstar. TIP lost a little more than 10% that year, while Vanguard’s short-duration VTIP declined a comparatively smaller 2.84%, despite inflation hitting 40-year highs in 2022.
VTIP Vs. TIP: Could Short Duration Have the Edge?
This is where shorter-duration strategies could gain attention. VTIP and STIP offer exposure to inflation-protected Treasuries with shorter maturities, potentially limiting the price sensitivity associated with rising real yields compared with broader-duration alternatives such as TIP.
The distinction matters if Waller’s hawkish stance translates into a sustained tightening cycle rather than a one-off policy adjustment.
For investors, the question is whether the inflation adjustments offered by TIPS can outweigh the pressure of rising real yields.
As the Fed’s inflation fight intensifies, TIPS ETFs deserve a closer look, but investors may need to pay as much attention to duration as to inflation itself.
TIP Price Action: iShares TIPS Bond ETF shares were up 0.13% at $104.97 at last check Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Despite CPI rising 6.5% in the 12 months through December 2022, the Morningstar US TIPS Index declined approximately 12% that year, according to Morningstar. TIP lost a little more than 10% that year, while Vanguard’s short-duration VTIP declined a comparatively smaller 2.84%, despite inflation hitting 40-year highs in 2022.

VTIP Vs. TIP: Could Short Duration Have the Edge?

This is where shorter-duration strategies could gain attention. VTIP and STIP offer exposure to inflation-protected Treasuries with shorter maturities, potentially limiting the price sensitivity associated with rising real yields compared with broader-duration alternatives such as TIP.

The distinction matters if Waller’s hawkish stance translates into a sustained tightening cycle rather than a one-off policy adjustment.

For investors, the question is whether the inflation adjustments offered by TIPS can outweigh the pressure of rising real yields.

As the Fed’s inflation fight intensifies, TIPS ETFs deserve a closer look, but investors may need to pay as much attention to duration as to inflation itself.

title: Binance Wins Court Order to Recover 45% of Its Stolen Funds
description:
Binance won a court order to reclaim frozen hack crypto, while the US holds $1.2 billion of the $6.3 billion stolen.
The post Binance Wins Court Order to Recover 45% of Its Stolen Funds appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Binance has secured a court order in Abu Dhabi to recover cryptocurrency frozen after its $6.3 billion hack last month.

According to Binance, customer assets are now fully covered. The exchange confirmed last week that it had replaced all affected assets using its own funds, including its emergency reserves.

This means customers no longer have to wait for the stolen crypto to be recovered before their balances are backed.

Withdrawals are also returning to normal. Binance reopened withdrawals across 87 networks and aims to restore the remaining services by the end of this week.

How Much of the $6.3 Billion Can Binance Recover?

The latest Abu Dhabi court ruling gives Binance another legal route to recover stolen funds.

Around $2.85 billion was previously frozen or intercepted, including assets blocked by stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle.

“We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets,” said Binance deputy general counsel Dugan Bliss.

Meanwhile, the US Justice Department has secured authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the frozen assets. Their eventual return remains uncertain.

The remaining billions are harder to recover. The FBI blames North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking group, which has allegedly been moving stolen funds across blockchains to hide their origin.

“Freezing assets and recovering them are two very different things,” Recoveris intelligence chief Roman Bieda told CBS News.

The exchange says it has covered customer losses, while the recovery of the stolen billions could take considerably longer.

title: Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft
A Scottish hacker tied to Scattered Spider was sentenced to six years in U.S. prison for a SIM-swap and phishing scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto.
This post Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft

A Scottish hacker tied to the Scattered Spider group was sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison on Tuesday for a text-message phishing and SIM-swapping scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California said.

Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month sentence from U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana. He had pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A restitution hearing is set for Dec. 11.

Prosecutors did not say which cryptocurrencies were taken, and the release does not break the haul down by coin. Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, closing out a prosecution of a hacker crew that the Justice Department charged together.

How the scheme worked

From September 2021 to April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen companies, prosecutors said. The messages posed as the employer or one of its IT contractors and linked to fake login pages that captured usernames, passwords and other personal information.

The group then used the stolen data to run SIM swaps, which move a victim’s phone number to a SIM card the attacker controls. That gave them a way into victims’ virtual currency accounts and wallets. The BBC reported that Buchanan set up a Telegram bot to collect the credentials as workers handed them over.

The largest single theft, according to prosecutors, was $1.67 million taken from one victim in December 2022. Prosecutors said the thefts had “severe, life-altering consequences” for victims.

The BBC said the money came from individual victims rather than from the companies whose employees were phished. Prosecutors first put the hacker group’s take at about $8 million, and the $11.6 million figure is the loss authorities calculated for the full scheme.

From Scotland to a California courtroom

Police Scotland searched Buchanan’s bedroom in April 2023 after a request from the FBI, the BBC said. Investigators found a device holding the names and addresses of victims, along with crypto seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim.

Buchanan left the U.K. the following month. Spanish authorities arrested him at Palma de Mallorca Airport in 2024 as he tried to board a private flight to Naples.

Bloomberg News reported, and Reuters relayed, that he was extradited from Spain in April 2025. He was charged with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft alongside four other alleged Scattered Spider members, and he has been in U.S. custody since.

What Scattered Spider is

Reuters has described Scattered Spider as a loose-knit community of hackers suspected of breaking into dozens of U.S. companies. The DOJ release does not use the group’s name, but the BBC says Buchanan, a teenage hacker when the campaign began, was a member and a Justice Department spokesperson has previously tied the defendants to it.

The BBC said Buchanan’s four co-defendants have all pleaded guilty and are serving time. It described the case as a years-long investigation involving authorities in the U.K., the U.S., Spain and Canada.

Scattered Spider has also faced prosecution in Britain. Two other members were jailed in the U.K. in July for a series of attacks, including one on Transport for London that caused £39 million in damage, the BBC said.

The judge will set the amount of restitution at a hearing on Dec. 11, the final step in the case against the Scottish hacker.

This post Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Wall Street Says the AI Trade Is Over — ETF Investors Aren’t Acting Like It
description:
Fears of an AI bubble bursting are gaining traction, but ETF investors appear to be sending a more complicated signal. 
While concerns about NVIDIA Corp’s (NASDAQ:NVDA) leadership turmoil and the sustainability of massive AI capital expenditure have weighed on sentiment, billions of dollars continue to flow into technology-focused ETFs.
       • VanEck Semiconductor ETF shares are consolidating. What’s the outlook for SMH shares?
The Kobeissi Letter, in a post on X, highlighted the cautious sentiment of AI investors: “Because of a personal event involving Jensen Huang, there are now widespread calls that the ‘AI bubble has popped.'”
“Sentiment is as though AI has failed, the investment wave is over, and we are in a global depression,” it said. The post continues after that.


Take a look at sentiment right now.
Because of a personal event involving Jensen Huang, there are now widespread calls that the "AI bubble has popped."
Sentiment is as though AI has failed, the investment wave is over, and we are in a global depression.
In reality? The S&P 500…
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 18, 2026





The latest fund-flow data suggest investors are not abandoning the AI trade entirely. Instead, they appear to be selectively adding exposure to semiconductor stocks and disruptive technology while becoming more cautious about software and other speculative growth segments.
According to ETFThemes data as of Wednesday, four ETFs — the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH), iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX), ARK Innovation ETF (BATS:ARKK) and ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (BATS:ARKW) — attracted approximately $14 billion in combined one-month inflows, despite losing between 12.8% and 14.8% over the same period.
The semiconductor trade remains particularly interesting. SMH attracted $5.11 billion over one month, while SOXX collected another $2.79 billion, even as both ETFs declined approximately 14% or more. However, the latest weekly figures reveal some hesitation. SOXX recorded $4.68 billion in outflows, while SMH attracted just $108 million, suggesting that dip-buying conviction may be weakening.
Investors Are Becoming More Selective About AI
The divergence becomes clearer when software ETFs enter the picture. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (BATS:IGV) experienced $1.48 billion in one-month outflows, suggesting investors are less willing to maintain exposure to the broader technology growth trade.
Meanwhile, the First Trust Nasdaq Artificial Intelligence and Robotics ETF (NYSE:BAI) attracted $663 million, indicating continued interest in dedicated AI exposure. However, the broader thematic ETF universe recorded approximately $6.7 billion in net redemptions outside the four leading inflow recipients.
This selective positioning comes against a backdrop of growing institutional caution. Bank of America’s November fund manager survey, cited by Reuters, found that investors’ net overweight allocation to technology stocks fell to 12% from 37% a month earlier. A record 38% of respondents also believed companies were overinvesting, while 52% expected an AI hyperscaler to announce capital expenditure cuts within six months. Reuters
The Next AI Trade May Look Different
The numbers suggest that investors are distinguishing between companies directly exposed to AI infrastructure spending and businesses whose valuations depend on broader expectations of AI adoption.
For ETF investors, the distinction matters. Semiconductor ETFs continue to attract substantial monthly capital despite steep losses, but recent weekly withdrawals show that conviction is not uniform.
Rather than interpreting every AI-related sell-off as an opportunity, investors should watch whether semiconductor inflows stabilize, whether software redemptions persist and whether capital broadens into other AI beneficiaries.
The AI trade may not be over, but the days when investors bought almost anything carrying an AI label could be numbered.

title: Republican senator blocks Trump's judicial nominee as Democrats prepare to take over
description:
By Nate Raymond and David Morgan 
   WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump's efforts to secure Senate confirmation of as many conservative judges as possible before Democrats take control of the chamber suffered a setback on Wednesday after ‌a Republican senator blocked one of his nominees from advancing. 
   Outgoing Republican Senator John Cornyn of Texas withheld support for US ‌Department of Justice official T. Elliot Gaiser to appear before the Senate Judiciary Committee for a hearing on Wednesday where it could take up his nomination to be a ​federal judge in Dallas. 
   Cornyn's decision not to return a so-called blue slip backing Gaiser marked the latest instance of a Republican senator not supporting a White House-backed judicial nominee in their home state during the lame-duck session before Democrats take control of the Senate on January 3. 
   "He's not from Texas," Cornyn told Reuters. "He has no trial experience, and the White House was trying to jam him down our throat without adequate ‌vetting for a lifetime job." 
   A White House official ⁠in a statement said it expects all of Trump's judicial nominees to be confirmed by year's end. 
   Senators traditionally help choose nominees for vacancies on federal courts in their states. By Senate custom, they can effectively veto ⁠trial court nominees they oppose in their states by refusing to return a blue slip, a form used to signal support. 
   Trump nominated Gaiser, 37, to a seat on the US District Court for the Northern District of Texas after the election. 
   The former Ohio solicitor general previously clerked for conservative US ​Supreme ​Court Justice Samuel Alito and currently heads the Justice Department's Office of ​Legal Counsel, a key unit that has frequently signed ‌off on the legality of his administration's actions. 
   Cornyn, a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee who lost a primary to a Trump-backed challenger, during Wednesday's hearing expressed support for Trump's decision to separately nominate Texas Supreme Court Justice James Sullivan to serve as a federal judge after he was defeated by a Democrat in the recent election. 
   But Cornyn has been pushing for the White House to pick someone else for the seat Gaiser was nominated to fill, recommending instead former federal prosecutor Steve Fahey of Texas. 
   "And the White House now seems to ‌be showing some interest in that," Cornyn said in an interview. 
   Republican Senator Ted ​Cruz of Texas, who supports Gaiser, in a statement warned that the White ​House has indicated that it would be "impossible for a brand-new ​nominee to complete the FBI background check fast enough to be confirmed." 
   "If the Senate Judiciary Committee does not ‌move Gaiser forward, the people of Texas will pay ​the price because it will effectively ​give the judicial seat to the Democrats, who will keep it vacant in perpetuity," Cruz said. 
   Two of Trump's other judicial nominees similarly ran into resistance from Republican senators in their home states after the midterm elections. 
   The White House on November 10 rescinded ​US District Judge Lee Rudofsky's nomination to the ‌8th US Circuit Court of Appeals and nominated Arkansas Supreme Court Justice J. Cody Hiland in his place following opposition ​from Arkansas' Republican senator. Hiland appeared at Wednesday's hearing with six other nominees. 
   (Reporting by Nate Raymond in Boston and ​David Morgan in Washington; Editing by Bill Berkrot and Alistair Bell) 
This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/republican-senator-cornyn-blocks-trump-173537955.html

Cornyn's decision not to return a so-called blue slip backing Gaiser marked the latest instance of a Republican senator not supporting a White House-backed judicial nominee in their home state during the lame-duck session before Democrats take control of the Senate on January 3.

"He's not from Texas," Cornyn told Reuters. "He has no trial experience, and the White House was trying to jam him down our throat without adequate ‌vetting for a lifetime job."

A White House official ⁠in a statement said it expects all of Trump's judicial nominees to be confirmed by year's end.

Senators traditionally help choose nominees for vacancies on federal courts in their states. By Senate custom, they can effectively veto ⁠trial court nominees they oppose in their states by refusing to return a blue slip, a form used to signal support.

Trump nominated Gaiser, 37, to a seat on the US District Court for the Northern District of Texas after the election.

The former Ohio solicitor general previously clerked for conservative US ​Supreme ​Court Justice Samuel Alito and currently heads the Justice Department's Office of ​Legal Counsel, a key unit that has frequently signed ‌off on the legality of his administration's actions.

Cornyn, a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee who lost a primary to a Trump-backed challenger, during Wednesday's hearing expressed support for Trump's decision to separately nominate Texas Supreme Court Justice James Sullivan to serve as a federal judge after he was defeated by a Democrat in the recent election.

But Cornyn has been pushing for the White House to pick someone else for the seat Gaiser was nominated to fill, recommending instead former federal prosecutor Steve Fahey of Texas.

"And the White House now seems to ‌be showing some interest in that," Cornyn said in an interview.

Republican Senator Ted ​Cruz of Texas, who supports Gaiser, in a statement warned that the White ​House has indicated that it would be "impossible for a brand-new ​nominee to complete the FBI background check fast enough to be confirmed."

"If the Senate Judiciary Committee does not ‌move Gaiser forward, the people of Texas will pay ​the price because it will effectively ​give the judicial seat to the Democrats, who will keep it vacant in perpetuity," Cruz said.

Two of Trump's other judicial nominees similarly ran into resistance from Republican senators in their home states after the midterm elections.

The White House on November 10 rescinded ​US District Judge Lee Rudofsky's nomination to the ‌8th US Circuit Court of Appeals and nominated Arkansas Supreme Court Justice J. Cody Hiland in his place following opposition ​from Arkansas' Republican senator. Hiland appeared at Wednesday's hearing with six other nominees.

(Reporting by Nate Raymond in Boston and ​David Morgan in Washington; Editing by Bill Berkrot and Alistair Bell)

title: Caterpillar's 'Best-In-Class' Construction Business Is Getting Overlooked, Analyst Says
description:
Caterpillar Inc. (NYSE:CAT) remains undervalued given the growth prospects of its construction business, Bank of America Securities said in a note Wednesday.
BofA analyst Michael Feniger reiterated a Buy rating and maintained a $746 price forecast following Caterpillar’s Compact Construction event Tuesday.
The analyst highlighted significant growth opportunities in compact equipment, rental operations and infrastructure projects.
Construction Business Remains Undervalued
BofA’s sum-of-the-parts analysis suggests investors are assigning a discount to Caterpillar’s construction business.
Feniger pointed to the recently announced joint venture between CNH Industrial and Kobelco, valued at approximately 10 times EBITDA. Feniger believes the transaction establishes a valuation floor for Caterpillar’s Construction Industries segment.
Caterpillar’s forward price-to-earnings multiple has contracted from approximately 30 times to 17 times in recent months as sentiment surrounding artificial intelligence weakened.
"CAT’s construction unit is a best-in-class leader that is gaining share," Feniger wrote, arguing that Wall Street’s preoccupation with artificial intelligence is overshadowing Caterpillar’s long-term construction growth potential.
The analyst also believes investors value Caterpillar’s Power & Energy segment at the very low end of its engine and turbine peers’ valuations, despite its high-quality portfolio, services and diverse end markets.
Compact Equipment Offers Significant Growth Potential
Caterpillar currently engages with only about 13% of the compact equipment market, leaving the remaining 87% as a potential growth opportunity.
The company expects to complete its North American rollout of its compact equipment strategy by early 2028, followed by international expansion by the end of that year.
Caterpillar is also strengthening its rental operations to attract new customers and drive equipment sales.
Meanwhile, the company’s major projects initiative is supporting a $4.2 billion transmission project in Nevada.
Citing the Texas Tribune, Feniger noted that Texas environmental regulators had resumed reviewing data center permits following an earlier freeze ordered by Gov. Greg Abbott. However, uncertainty surrounding the midterm elections remains a risk to Caterpillar’s power business.
2027 Outlook Remains Positive Despite Risks
BofA expects Caterpillar to benefit from infrastructure spending, equipment replacement demand and continued expansion in rental and services operations.
However, Feniger cautioned that pricing pressure, dealer inventory reductions, unfavorable tariff policies and potential capital spending delays among mining and oil and gas customers could weigh on Caterpillar’s outlook.
The analyst forecasts adjusted earnings of $26.75 per share in 2026, rising to $33.50 in 2027 and $42 in 2028.
BofA’s $746 price forecast reflects a valuation of approximately 22 times estimated 2027 earnings.
That exceeds Caterpillar’s 15-year historical valuation range of 15 to 18 times earnings but remains within its recovery valuation range of 20 to 30 times earnings.
CAT Price Action: Caterpillar shares were down 2.48% at $556.63 at the time of publication on Wednesday. The stock is near its 52-week low of $537.08, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: Bitcoin Price Analysis: BTC at a Breaking Point as $63K Support Faces Critical Test
description: Bitcoin’s November sell-off has extended, and it now trades around $64K, down roughly 14% over the past week. Rising expectations of a Fed rate hike, persistent spot ETF outflows, and a tech-stock slide ahead of Nvidia’s earnings have weighed on risk assets. BTC has also closed below its 200-week moving average near $68K, so the […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin’s November sell-off has extended, and it now trades around $64K, down roughly 14% over the past week.

Rising expectations of a Fed rate hike, persistent spot ETF outflows, and a tech-stock slide ahead of Nvidia’s earnings have weighed on risk assets. BTC has also closed below its 200-week moving average near $68K, so the current demand zone has become a key test. Meanwhile, the Adjusted SOPR shows that holders are now realizing losses on average, a condition that has often appeared near previous local bottoms.

Bitcoin Price Analysis: The Daily Chart

On the daily timeframe, Bitcoin has given back almost all of its summer recovery. After two failed attempts to break the $86K–$90K supply zone in September and October, the price formed lower highs. It then lost the $78K–$81K order block and fell through the $68K demand zone with a series of large bearish candles.

BTC is now sitting on the $63K support. This level held the market during the June–August consolidation and served as the springboard for the August rally. A long lower wick toward $62K shows that buyers are responding, but the rebound has so far been shallow. A decisive daily close below this area would expose the $58K–$60K zone, which marks the July bottom, followed by the deeper $52K–$54K demand region.

The RSI has dropped to approximately 25, deep in oversold territory. Similar readings in February and June came before relief bounces. However, any recovery would first face the $68K level, now overhead supply that lines up with the 200-week moving average. Until buyers reclaim that area, the daily structure remains bearish.

BTC/USDT 4-Hour Chart

The 4-hour chart shows a clear downtrend that has been building since early October. The loss of $76K support in early November marked a turning point, and the decline then accelerated through the $68K–$70K zone. Since the November 14 flush toward $62K, Bitcoin has been moving sideways in a tight range just above the $63K demand zone.

Momentum has begun to improve slightly. The RSI has recovered from below 30 to about 40 and printed higher lows while price retested $63K, suggesting selling pressure is easing. A move above $66K could open the way for a relief rally toward the $68K–$70K supply zone, where sellers would likely become active again.

On the other hand, a clean breakdown below $63K would invalidate the current base-building attempt and would likely send the price toward $60K. For now, the short-term pattern points to consolidation within a broader downtrend, and the next directional move depends on whether buyers can keep defending $63K.

On-Chain Analysis

The Adjusted Spent Output Profit Ratio (aSOPR) on CryptoQuant compares the selling price of moved coins with the price at which they were acquired. Readings above 1 indicate that coins are being sold at a profit on average, while readings below 1 indicate that holders are realizing losses.

The chart tracks its 30-day exponential moving average.

The metric peaked near 1.07 in late 2024 and has trended lower since, following Bitcoin’s broader decline. During 2026, sub-1 readings appeared in February and again in June–July, as BTC fell toward the $60K region. Both periods were followed by recoveries. The EMA then climbed back to approximately 1.01 during the rally toward $88K, but it has now dropped sharply below 0.99.

This shift suggests that recent buyers are capitulating and selling at a loss, which often helps wash out weak hands. However, the February episode shows that the metric can stay below 1 for weeks before a sustained rebound. A return above 1, combined with a successful defense of the $63K support, would offer stronger evidence that selling pressure has run its course.

The post Bitcoin Price Analysis: BTC at a Breaking Point as $63K Support Faces Critical Test appeared first on CryptoPotato.

title: Fed Minutes Reveal a Bigger Rate Hike Was on the Table Before Inflation Ran Hot
description:
Fed minutes show officials floated a bigger rate hike in October. Traders still bet on a quarter point. See why.
The post Fed Minutes Reveal a Bigger Rate Hike Was on the Table Before Inflation Ran Hot appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Federal Reserve officials floated a rate hike bigger than a quarter point in October, minutes released Wednesday show. Their trigger was bad inflation data, and it has since arrived.

That puts a half-point hike back in play for December 9. A bigger move would raise borrowing costs for homebuyers, companies, and AI firms behind this month’s stock sell-off. Bitcoin and gold slipped after the release.

How Close Did the Fed Come to Hiking in October?

The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on October 28 in a 10-2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted a quarter-point hike.

The minutes show the split ran wider. “Some” officials favored a hike. A few who backed the hold called it a close call.

“A couple of participants noted that an increase of more than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable.”

The data turned unfavorable. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above forecasts, in a hot US CPI report. Employers added 165,000 jobs against 65,000 expected.

On Wednesday, Governor Christopher Waller called for a half-point hike. The minutes show he was not the first to raise it.

Why Are Traders Still Betting on a Quarter Point?

Traders priced a 95% chance of a December hike shortly before the release, per CME FedWatch. Odds of a half point sat at just 5.3%, up from 3.1% a day earlier.

The 10-year Treasury yield holds above 5%, and tech stocks led a $2.2 trillion global sell-off on November 16.

In the minutes, almost all officials discussed what happens if AI investments disappoint. Most said AI debt had grown through “complex and opaque financing structures.”

Still, a jumbo hike is not the consensus. Hammack has called for steady quarter-point steps. A number of officials also said closer scrutiny of AI spending could cool inflation on its own.

Officials meet December 8 and 9. A half-point hike would land on the same AI borrowers the Fed now flags as a risk, and Fed staff warn hedge fund leverage could spread a sell-off.

title: GTA 6 Is Winning Over Gamers: Can Take-Two Stock Beat Bitcoin Next?
description:
GTA 6 set a video-game preorder record, which begs the question: does Take-Two Interactive (NASDAQ:TTWO) stock now look like a better bet than Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC)?
GTA 6’s Preorder Record, by the Numbers
Sensor Tower’s preorder estimate crossed $1.1 billion, then hit $1.54 billion on 15.88 million digital preorders by Nov. 17, before topping $1.65 billion a day later. 
Reuters separately put units sold at roughly 17.1 million early Wednesday as regional launches began, though that $1.65 billion is an outside estimate of consumer spending, not Take-Two’s own bookings.
GTA 6 is also backing up the hype with a 99 on Metacritic, tying "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time" for the highest-rated game ever, with perfect or near-perfect scores from outlets including IGN, GameSpot and Forbes.
Wall Street’s Targets Don’t Agree With Each Other
Analysts can’t agree on how big this gets, with Oppenheimer expecting about 20 million copies and $1.85 billion in revenue over the first three days while keeping its $280 target, and B. Riley expecting 43.5 million copies by the March quarter with a $300 target. 
Wells Fargo went furthest, raising its estimate to 65 million copies and $9.76 billion in bookings, which is $1.66 billion above the midpoint of Take-Two’s own $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion guidance for fiscal 2027.
GTA V backs up the optimism, having sold nearly 235 million copies and still growing in spending 13 years later. 
But GTA 6 launched with single-player only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, there’s still no date for multiplayer or a PC version, and the free month of GTA+ included with preorders hasn’t yet turned into paid subscriptions. 
The next real number to watch is Take-Two’s December-quarter bookings, guided at $3.35 billion to $3.50 billion.
What Price Does Bitcoin Need to Win This Matchup?
Take-Two traded at $215 Wednesday morning, up 7.5% on the week, and that rally already ate into the stock’s upside, with Oppenheimer’s $280 target now pointing to about 28% more gains.
Bitcoin traded near $63,000 the same morning, and even after Citi trimmed its 12-month target to $99,532 from $113,000, that lower number still points to 56% upside, more than either Take-Two target offers.
Bitcoin’s real problem right now is demand, with U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs seeing $239.9 million in net outflows Nov. 17, most of it from BlackRock’s IBIT, as Citi pointed to weaker fund demand, a stronger dollar and higher real yields. 
Grayscale’s Zach Pandl sees it differently, calling the token’s roughly 17% drop this month a good entry point for longer-term buyers.
Bitcoin doesn’t need to hit $100,000 to beat a $280 Take-Two target. It just needs to climb back to about $81,300.
Image: Shutterstock

title: Bitget Opens Tokenized ETF Onchain Yield Without a DeFi Wallet
description:

The post Bitget Opens Tokenized ETF Onchain Yield Without a DeFi Wallet appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
Bitget launched rToken Earn on November 16, 2026, opening tokenized ETF onchain yield for Reality-issued rSPY and rQQQ. Eligible non-U.S. users in permitted jurisdictions can earn variable vault income. They keep exposure to the underlying S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 ETF trackers. Subscriptions run through Bitget Earn. Users do not open a separate DeFi wallet or talk to vault contracts themselves.

The Bitget release frames the product as the next use of rTokens after trading and collateral. Bitget handles subscriptions and redemptions on the user's behalf, with no fixed term. Yields are variable and not guaranteed. Availability still depends on jurisdiction and eligibility.

How Tokenized ETF Onchain Yield Moves on Subscribe

The puzzle is not that index ETFs can sit as tokens. Brokers and crypto venues have sold equity-like exposure through wrappers for years. The claim here is narrower. A 1:1-backed tokenized ETF claim can leave the trade screen and enter programmable lending rails. The holder does not have to become a DeFi operator.

Reality issues the rTokens and says each unit is backed 1:1 by the corresponding securities held through its custody path. Ember Protocol supplies the vault infrastructure. Fluid supplies the lending markets and liquidity the strategy uses. Bitget sits in front as the account layer that takes the order, routes the deposit, and brings back the redemption.

Follow one subscription through the stack. An eligible user holds rSPY or rQQQ in a Bitget account. That user joins the matching Earn vault. Bitget moves the tokens into the Ember vault path. The strategy places that collateral into Fluid lending markets. Any yield that returns is variable product income, not a fixed coupon. It is also not a promise that the index return itself is enhanced.

That is tokenized ETF onchain yield as plumbing. Index exposure stays the claim. Income is a separate lending overlay on the same tokens.

Why the Rails Matter, and Where the Catch Sits

Tokenized equities only change capital markets if the claim can do more than trade. Trade and collateral already proved demand for rTokens. Bitget cites DeFiLlama Research figures of more than $1.86 billion in cumulative rToken trading volume between June and July 2026. In October it added rToken Stock Transfer, a two-step path for eligible users to convert supported brokerage holdings into rTokens. Earn is the income layer on top of that catalogue.

Bitwise Investment Manager, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Bitwise Asset Management, is set to curate the vault strategy. That curation service is not live at launch. Bitget says it will roll out later. Until then, the live surfaces are Ember vaults, Fluid lending, Reality issuance, and Bitget's Earn front end.

"An asset should not be limited to just one purpose," Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the release. Jonathan Man, portfolio manager at Bitwise, called tokenization the first step and putting the assets to work the next one. Ember co-founder Ibra Barbery framed the point as infrastructure users should not have to think about. Fluid founder and CEO Samyak Jain cast lending as the engine that now reaches widely held traditional assets onchain.

The catch is the usual one for AI and blockchain readers watching tokenization infra. A packaged Earn product hides wallet friction. It does not hide smart-contract, oracle, liquidity, or counterparty risk on the vault and lending path. U.S. persons stay outside. Yield is not guaranteed. Bitwise curation is still ahead of the switch. The release also skips a live APY and a TVL figure for the new vaults. It gives no independent proof of how deep Fluid liquidity is for these tokens on day one.

What Is Proven, and What Is Not

What the primary record shows is concrete. Bitget opened rToken Earn for rSPY and rQQQ on November 16, 2026. Reality issues the tokens with a 1:1 securities-backing claim. Ember and Fluid are named as vault and lending rails. Access runs through Bitget Earn for eligible non-U.S. users. Bitwise strategy curation is disclosed as a later rollout.

What remains open is harder. The launch does not prove durable income versus holding the cash-market ETFs. It also does not prove every eligible jurisdiction will keep the product available as rules shift. It does not prove that tokenized index claims behave like registered fund shares in every local legal sense once they sit in a lending vault.

The sharper model is simple. Tokenized ETF onchain yield here is not a new index fund. It is custody-backed index tokens plugged into programmable collateral rails behind an exchange account. Watch whether Bitwise curation arrives. Watch whether vault balances grow past launch marketing. Watch whether the same Earn path widens beyond rSPY and rQQQ without forcing users back into a separate DeFi wallet.

The post Bitget Opens Tokenized ETF Onchain Yield Without a DeFi Wallet appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.

title: Important Ripple News and XRP Price Update: November 18
description: A breakdown of the latest Ripple ecosystem advancements and an update on XRP's recent price movements.
fullContent:
Ripple remains among the most discussed names in the cryptocurrency space thanks to ongoing ecosystem developments, while its cross-border token XRP continues to attract the attention of traders and investors.

Here are some of the latest news and events surrounding the company and its native asset.

The Biggest Swell Yet

Ripple recently held what it described as its largest Swell event to date. The gathering brought together developers, researchers, XRP community members, and financial leaders to discuss the future of on-chain finance.

More than 1,500 attendees participated in New York, while the company revealed that over 1,700 institutions, corporates, and enterprises now use its solutions.

Ripple also highlighted the rapid growth of the tokenized asset sector, which has already expanded into a market worth roughly $400 billion, and emphasized a decade of work building “the Internet of Value, with XRP Ledger as the foundation.”

Another Milestone for XRPL

The XRP Ledger Foundation recently completed the attestation of the XRP Ledger against the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

“It is the first public, permissionless layer-1 blockchain to have the toolkit’s Architecture and Resiliency principles independently verified,” the announcement reads.

The framework was created through cooperation between global financial institutions and policymakers and is designed to evaluate networks used for tokenized assets. For banks and asset managers, the verification serves as an additional standards-based reference when assessing the XRP Ledger.

Evernorth’s XRP Write-Down

Another Ripple-related headline arrived from Evernorth Holdings. As CryptoPotato recently reported, the entity significantly reduced the accounting value of its XRP reserves, recording roughly $505 million in impairment charges.

Importantly, this was now caused by actual sales of the asset. The write-down stemmed from accounting requirements that force companies to adjust the carrying value of digital assets when prices decline below their acquisition cost.

Despite the move, Evernorth Holdings remains committed to its XRP-focused strategy and continues expanding operations around the token via key partnerships.

ETF Demand is Nowhere to Be Seen

Institutional appetite toward XRP appears to have dried up lately. After attracting considerable inflows for months, spot XRP ETFs entered a quiet period, followed by renewed outflows.

This is generally viewed as a bearish signal since a prolonged absence of fresh capital may weigh on market sentiment and limit the asset’s upside potential.

Companies offering such investment vehicles include financial giants like Franklin Templeton, Canary Capital, Bitwise, Grayscale, and 21Shares. Cumulative net inflows to the spot XRP ETFs to date stand at around $1.78 billion.

XRP Price Outlook

Ripple’s cross-border token was negatively impacted by the latest market crash, briefly tumbling to around $0.90 last weekend. The bulls reclaimed some lost ground in the following days, with XRP temporarily surpassing the $1 barrier before plunging to the current $0.98 (per CMC).

According to Tranquility Crypto, “XRP is trying to make a decision here.” The analyst noted that the price has been printing lower highs since the $3.60 region and is now back at a major demand zone, which can precede a major rally.

For his part, Ali Martinez suggested that XRP could bottom at around $0.78. He believes that if that level holds, the asset can begin a significant recovery toward $3.50.
