title: Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds
Binance says it has a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to recover crypto frozen after the $6.3 billion hack.
This post Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds

Binance says it has secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to help it recover crypto frozen after the record $6.3 billion hack last month, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The exchange has not said how much of the money the order covers.

Reuters described Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) as Binance’s main financial regulator. Binance deputy general counsel Dugan Bliss confirmed the order in a statement but gave no details on its terms. Neither the company nor Reuters said which assets it applies to.

“We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Bliss said.

What is frozen

Binance has said about $2.85 billion of the stolen tokens were frozen or intercepted after the Oct. 29 attack, according to its own incident report. That is roughly 45% of the $6.34 billion it says was affected.

Most of it sits with stablecoin issuers. Tether said it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of the attack, and Circle said it froze about $1.1 billion in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. Circle added that it does not decide who owns frozen assets, a question it left to law enforcement and the courts.

The Justice Department has separately obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the stolen crypto. It is part of more than $2.7 billion that Justice says government and private-sector efforts have frozen. Criminal Division head A. Tysen Duva said the department helped “immediately halt about half of this historic breach.” Reuters did not say how the ADGM order fits with the U.S. action.

How the hack unfolded

Binance says the attack began months earlier, with a tampered software installer that compromised one engineer in June. In September, another engineer was approached by a fake recruiter and persuaded to run a bogus interview assignment that installed malware, the company said.

From there, the attackers reached an internal wallet-signing service and drained Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. The thefts included 233.46 million XRP, about 970,500 SOL and 18,270 BTC, according to Binance.

The FBI has attributed the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Binance has said the same. Pyongyang denies involvement. Blockchain analysts said the attacker tried to outrun the freezes by swapping stablecoins into ether over about 20 minutes, but the issuers moved faster.

That split matters for bitcoin. Tether and Circle can block their own tokens, but bitcoin has no issuer. The stolen BTC is not covered by those freezes and can be stopped only if it reaches an exchange or service that blocks it.

Binance says it can absorb the loss

Binance has already said it replaced the affected assets with company funds, using part of its SAFU emergency fund and its corporate treasury. Withdrawals resumed in phases earlier this month, and the exchange aims to reopen all remaining networks and assets by the end of this week, Reuters reported.

On Wednesday, Binance’s Asia-Pacific head SB Seker told Reuters at the Singapore FinTech Festival that the company plans to expand into five Asian markets in 2027 and does not need to raise new funds. He said talks are under way with five or six markets, three of them at a mature stage, and details are due in the first quarter.

Seker said the cost of replacing the stolen tokens was “statistically” not a large amount for the company. “In terms of the impact to us, we can take the impact and we can weather it without any change to the way we operate,” he said.

This post Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: SHIB Falls to $0.0000038 as Its First Death Cross in 14 Months Lands
description: Shiba Inu broke its July low and printed its first death cross in 14 months. Here is why support near $0.0000035 decides whether the oversold slide finds a floor.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Shiba Inu has slipped under its July low, and its chart printed the first death cross in 14 months.
  • Daily momentum sits deep in oversold territory, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • The nearest floor near $0.0000035 now decides whether the slide finds a footing.

Shiba Inu extended its yearly slide this week as a closely watched bearish signal appeared on its chart. The 50-day average crossed under the 200-day line for the first time since last year.

The signal lands as Shibarium activity fades and tax-loss selling season approaches. Traders want to know if an oversold token can stage a relief bounce before year end.

Shiba Inu Slips Under Its July Low as Network Use Fades

A death cross forms when the 50-day moving average drops under the 200-day average. Traders read it as a sign that a downtrend has taken hold. The token is now down about 45% this year, and crypto analyst Sam Daodu has flagged room for further losses.

Demand on the network looks thin. Shibarium, the project's layer-2 chain, handled only 691 transactions on Nov 10. That was well under half its daily average of 1,624 over the prior month. Exchange balances remain heavy. CryptoQuant data showed 86.2 trillion SHIB on exchanges as of Nov 8. Coins parked on exchanges are easy to sell.

The weakness extends well beyond SHIB. Dogecoin has lost about 50% this year, while bitcoin is down nearly 27%. Year-end tax rules could add pressure. US investors can sell losers before Dec 31 to offset gains and up to $3,000 of ordinary income.

Both Key Averages Now Sit Well Above the Price

Shiba Inu (SHIB) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

SHIB traded near $0.0000038 on Monday, down about 2% over the past day. The token now sits under both of its key moving averages.

A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the underlying trend. The 50-day average stands near $0.0000047, well above the current price. The 200-day average sits higher still, around $0.0000053. When price trades below both lines, each one tends to act as a ceiling on rallies.

The shorter average now sits beneath the longer one, so recent prices are weaker than the longer-run trend.

Selling has also sped up. SHIB lost about 24% over the past 30 days, and roughly 15% came in the last week alone.

Overhead, the old July support near $0.00000405 has turned into resistance. Traders who bought there may now sell to get out near breakeven. That level sits just above the price and marks the first test for any bounce.

Oversold Readings Have Not Stopped the Selling

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, has dropped to about 27. Readings below 30 count as oversold. They show that selling has run hard and fast, and stretched markets often snap back with a relief bounce.

The other signals still favor sellers. Momentum keeps pointing down, with the MACD below its signal line. Trend-strength readings confirm a real downtrend. Any rally from here would run against that trend, so it could fade quickly.

July showed how fast SHIB can turn. The token traded near $0.00000418 on Jul 24 and jumped more than a quarter in just two days. That move came from a similar washed-out setup.

Still, oversold conditions can last for weeks in a strong downtrend, and a low RSI does not mark the bottom. Buyers would need to show up in size before a bounce could stick.

$0.0000035 Is the Floor Bulls Cannot Lose

Support sits below the Nov 14 dip, when SHIB briefly touched around $0.0000037. The data maps no further support beneath it. A clean break there would leave the token in open air, with no clear level to catch a fall.

Upside has its own hurdles. First resistance sits near $0.0000043. A close above it would undo the July-low breakdown and trap late sellers. The next ceiling stands around $0.0000048, close to the 50-day average. Bulls would need real volume to push through both.

Daodu sees room for one more leg down. He said SHIB could slip about 3% to retest the recent dip without breaking the floor.

His outlook improves only under two conditions. Shibarium activity would need to climb back to its recent daily average. SHIB would also need to close back above the July low. Until then, he expects the token to stay capped below that old support into the new year.

What Could Flip the Next Three Days

SHIB's path likely hinges on a few nearby levels.

  • Bullish: An oversold bounce that reclaims the former July support would hand buyers their first win in weeks. That move would put first resistance in play as the next target. The setup fails if SHIB drops back under the Nov 14 dip.
  • Bearish: A daily close below the nearest support would extend the slide, with no mapped floor underneath. Sellers would then set the pace. A close back above the former July support would cancel this view.

Sellers Keep the Upper Hand Into Year End

For now, the trend and the network data both argue for patience. Sellers control the chart, and Shibarium has yet to show a recovery in demand.

Short sellers face their own danger. Deeply oversold tokens can rip higher without warning. A sudden squeeze could punish anyone who piles in late on the bearish side.

title: XRP Price Was Worth Less Than a Penny When GTA 5 Launched: Could GTA 6 See It Hit $100?
description:
XRP was trading below a cent when GTA5 arrived. Thirteen years later, GTA6 is going to be released while XRP has became a financial giant.
The post XRP Price Was Worth Less Than a Penny When GTA 5 Launched: Could GTA 6 See It Hit $100? appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
XRP price was trading below one cent when Grand Theft Auto V arrived in September 2013. Thirteen years later, Rockstar is preparing to release GTA 6, while XRP has grown into one of the largest cryptos. XRP is a financial giant today.

The comparison is striking. On September 17, 2013, the day GTA V launched, XRP was trading at $0.009613. Today, XRP trades near $0.95, representing a price gain of almost 100 times from that launch-day price.

But can XRP deliver another extraordinary rally as GTA 6 arrives? A $100 price target would turn a relatively small crypto investment into a fortune, but it would also require XRP to reach a market valuation never seen before in the crypto industry.

Xrp (XRP)
24h7d30d1yAll time

Discover: The Best Token Presales

From GTA 5 Penny-Stock Era to XRP Multi-Dollar Price Rally

When GTA V introduced players to Los Santos in 2013, XRP was still largely flying under the radar. Its price sat below one cent, and its market cap was ranging around $75 million. Then the following years changed everything.

XRP broke above $0.10 in May 2017 before accelerating during the historic crypto bull market. By December 2017, the token had crossed $1 and continued climbing toward its January 2018 all-time high of $3.84.

That is an extraordinary transformation from its GTA V launch-day price. A $1,000 investment at $0.009613 would have purchased more than 100,000 XRP. At $3.84, that position would have been worth nearly $400,000. Something that only crypto can do.

However, XRP’s journey was far from smooth. The token endured successive bear markets, regulatory uncertainty, and the SEC’s lawsuit against Ripple in December 2020. Its recovery eventually pushed XRP back toward record territory in 2025, when it reached $3.65.

Now, XRP is trading around $0.95, substantially below its previous peaks. Will another major recovery begin before GTA 6 is released?

GTA 6 Could Be the Start of XRP’s Next $100 Chapter

Rockstar’s GTA 6 arrives more than 13 years after GTA V, creating an interesting milestone for XRP investors. XRP has experienced multiple market cycles during the same period, transforming from a sub-penny asset into a major digital currency.

XRP currently has 63.5 billion tokens in circulation. At $100 per token, its market capitalization would reach $6.35 trillion. That would put XRP among the most valuable financial assets in the world, exceeding the market capitalization of most publicly traded companies.

The bullish argument rests on XRP’s potential to capture a much larger share of institutional payments, cross-border settlements, and digital asset liquidity. Ripple has spent years building financial infrastructure around the XRP Ledger, while institutional interest in crypto investment products continues to develop.

A stronger crypto market could also provide the liquidity needed for another substantial XRP rally. But XRP would need considerably more capital, adoption, and sustained demand to justify a multi-trillion-dollar valuation.

The historical comparison remains fascinating. XRP went from less than a penny when GTA V launched to several dollars during subsequent crypto cycles. People probably didn’t believe XRP would reach where it is now.

title: Florida Man Sentenced in North Carolina to 51 Months for $800,000 Cell Phone Tower Fraud Scheme
description:

Alexander Francise Blasscyk, 48, of Windermere, Florida, was sentenced in federal court in Charlotte, North Carolina, to 51 months in prison plus three years of […]
The post Florida Man Sentenced in North Carolina to 51 Months for $800,000 Cell Phone Tower Fraud Scheme appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
Federal prosecutors have secured a 51-month prison sentence against a Florida man who ran a fraudulent cell phone tower consulting scheme that collected more than $800,000 from hundreds of victims.

Alexander Francise Blasscyk, 48, of Windermere, Florida, was sentenced in federal court in Charlotte, North Carolina, to 51 months in prison plus three years of supervised release and ordered to pay $1,039,115.30 in restitution, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of North Carolina.

According to court documents, Blasscyk defrauded victims by falsely claiming to be a cell tower consultant. Between 2018 and 2024, he told individuals, including residents of Ashe County, that he would market their properties to cell tower companies and wireless carriers for a fee. He also promised to negotiate lease agreements that would allow the companies to build towers on their land in exchange for rental payments.

Hundreds of victims, including individuals and businesses, paid Blasscyk or companies he controlled more than $800,000 for the purported consulting services and related expenses. However, little to no work was performed. Blasscyk did not market the properties to wireless carriers or cell tower companies as promised, nor did he negotiate the lease agreements he had offered to secure.

To persuade victims to hand over their money, Blasscyk provided false and fraudulent documents through his company.

Blasscyk used two companies to solicit fees for nonexistent work marketing land for tower leases and instead spent the money on personal expenses, including hotels, short-term rentals, restaurants and bars.

U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson said the defendant gave people the hope of passive income.

“Blasscyk gave people the hope of passive income — making false promises to lease land to cell phone tower companies while collecting consulting fees. But Blasscyk did no consulting, made no such deals, and created fake documents to cover up his fraud.”

He pleaded guilty to wire fraud in October 2025.

title: Nuvera Opens All-Hours Polygon Stablecoin Settlement
description:
Polygon Labs said on November 18, 2026, that Nuvera Polygon stablecoin settlement is live on Open Money Stack. Customers can still fund dollar accounts by bank transfer. Then they can move the money onward as a stablecoin at any hour through the OMS dashboard. That path sits beside waiting on correspondent banking cutoffs. The Polygon […]
The post Nuvera Opens All-Hours Polygon Stablecoin Settlement appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
Polygon Labs said on November 18, 2026, that Nuvera Polygon stablecoin settlement is live on Open Money Stack. Customers can still fund dollar accounts by bank transfer. Then they can move the money onward as a stablecoin at any hour through the OMS dashboard. That path sits beside waiting on correspondent banking cutoffs. The Polygon Labs post is the primary record for the go-live.

That is the news. A cross-border payments firm kept the bank-transfer front door. It put the onchain hop behind it.

How Nuvera Polygon Stablecoin Settlement Works

Nuvera builds payments rails for importers, exporters, and firms that pay suppliers across regions. Its customers sit in the Americas, Europe, Asia, and Africa. The company says it uses local rails where they exist. It uses SWIFT where they do not. It uses stablecoins when faster settlement is the job. Its tagline frames the harder markets plainly: "Unbanked isn't unbankable."

With Polygon OMS, the customer path stays familiar at the start. A business pays in by bank transfer. The transfer lands in a dollar account Nuvera issues. Nuvera's team can then move the funds onward as a stablecoin. That hop runs through the OMS dashboard around the clock.

Marcelo Correa, Nuvera's Chief Business Officer, put the product test in one line in the Polygon post. Customers judge the firm on how quickly and predictably money arrives. Polygon OMS lets Nuvera settle in stablecoins. It keeps the bank-transfer experience those customers already expect.

What Polygon Open Money Stack Adds

Polygon Open Money Stack is Polygon's stack for moving money across bank accounts, cards, cash, and wallets. The pitch is one integration surface for payments companies. It is not a duct-taped rail for each step. That design sits in the same lane as earlier bank-to-stablecoin transfer experiments on Polygon rails.

On the outbound side, Polygon says OMS can send to bank accounts and cash pickup points. It can also send to wallets on Polygon, Ethereum, and Solana. Cash and debit cards sit on the pay-in side of the same stack. Agent payments with preset limits are part of the broader OMS story. They are not the Nuvera customer flow announced today.

The practical stake for Nuvera's users is timing. An overseas invoice may need to clear after a bank's cutoff. The onward leg can still settle in a stablecoin. The bank transfer still has to land. What changes after that landing is the settlement clock.

What a Bank-to-Stablecoin Settlement Path Is Actually Telling You

Here is the recurring question this go-live presses. When a private dollar token says it is worth one dollar, what does wiring it behind a bank pay-in prove?

It does not invent a new peg. It does not replace Nuvera's bank relationships. It proves a settlement handoff. Customers keep funding the way they already fund. The money can keep moving after banking hours. The next hop is onchain.

That is a different story from listing a stablecoin on an exchange. It is also different from parking float in DeFi. Cross-border payments firms get hired for speed and predictability. Correspondent banking cutoffs are the failure mode those customers already know. Today's launch is a bet on the bank-transfer front door. The back office can stop treating evening as a hard stop.

Unknowns remain. The Polygon post does not publish live settlement volumes or fee schedules. It also skips a full country list for Nuvera dollar accounts. It does not name which stablecoin tickers sit on every outbound route. Licensing claims and bank relationships stay high level. Production proof will show up in arrival times, not in the launch post.

The peg promise is still the same question it always was. Can a familiar bank pay-in feed an all-hours stablecoin settlement leg? And can it do that without asking the customer to become a crypto operator first?

title: Silver Price Erased 45 Years of Gains. Will It Crash Further?
description:
Silver price crashed 62% to a new 2026 low below its 1980 high. See 6 reasons behind the drop and key support levels.
The post Silver Price Erased 45 Years of Gains. Will It Crash Further? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
The silver price fell to $45.14 on Wednesday, a new 2026 low. The drop leaves silver 62% below its January record and back under its 1980 high.

Breakout buyers now sit on losses, and former support may now act as resistance.

Silver’s 45-Year Ceiling Failed to Hold

Barchart data shows silver trading back below the $50 zone that capped prices in 1980 and 2011.

Both peaks were nominal highs. Silver only cleared that zone in late 2025, and losing it suggests the entire breakout has unwound.

More Pain Ahead for Silver Investors?

On Wednesday, according to WhaleScan, platinum dropped 4.82%, silver 4.39%, copper 3.84%, palladium 3.41%, and gold 2.83%.

The account estimated that over $850 billion vanished from gold and silver in one day. That is a paper loss in market value, not cash leaving the market.

WhaleScan described the move as a forced liquidation phase driven by margin calls. It set $41.50 as the next target for silver.

The Nasdaq fell 2.5% on Monday, and metals were sold alongside tech stocks. That points to a rates shock hitting everything rather than a silver-specific panic.

Why Is the Silver Price Falling? 6 Key Drivers

  • Fed hike bets. CME FedWatch shows a 96.7% chance of a 25 basis point hike on December 9. October Consumer Price Index (CPI) data beat forecasts.
  • Strong dollar. The Dollar Index sits at a 19-month high near 103.5, with 10-year Treasury yields around 5.14%.
  • Liquidation. Investors sold metals to cover losses in stocks.
  • Solar slump. The Silver Institute expects solar silver demand to fall 19% in 2026, a record decline.
  • Fading investor demand. Silver held in exchange-traded products (ETPs) is down 55 million ounces this year, and buyers aren’t rushing in.
  • Gold outperformance. The gold/silver ratio climbed to about 82, from roughly 43 in January, even as gold hit a 14-month low.

Silver Price Outlook

Since January, the daily chart shows only lower highs and lower lows.

Silver has lost every key Fibonacci level, the ratio-based zones traders use to map support. The 0.786 level near $54.50 broke in late October, and a retest failed last week.

The price is now testing the October 28, 2025 low near $45.50. A daily close below it would confirm the breakdown.

However, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) has dropped below 30, into oversold territory. Its latest low also sits above the early November reading, while price made a lower low.

That hints at a possible bullish divergence, though it remains unconfirmed.

If $45.50 fails, the next supports sit at $41.50 and $36.20. A daily close back above $54.50 would invalidate the bearish structure.

The next test arrives with Wednesday’s Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes. Until rate expectations cool, silver’s path may depend more on the Fed than on industrial demand.

The post Silver Price Erased 45 Years of Gains. Will It Crash Further? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’
K33 Research said bitcoin is in "deep value territory" after a 14% weekly drop, as ETF outflows, liquidations and hedging demand reach levels seen near past bottoms.
This post Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’ first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’

K33 Research said bitcoin is trading in “deep value territory” after a 14% weekly drop, arguing that “any entry below $70K is a gift from the market” for medium- to long-term investors.

The call comes in the firm’s weekly report, “No gain, plenty of pain,” which published Nov. 16. Head of research Vetle Lunde wrote that bitcoin’s slide has erased its August and September gains and left the market deeply oversold. Bitcoin has posted six straight red weekly candles and is on track for a record 13 consecutive days of lower daily highs, according to K33.

Lunde said a streak of six weekly losses has happened only twice before, from Jan. 26 to March 1, 2026, and from April 3 to May 29, 2022. Daily RSI, a momentum gauge, hit 19.95 on Saturday and has stayed below 25 since Friday. Bitcoin also fell below its 200-week moving average, near $68,000, after its worst weekly return since June 7.

Bitcoin below its long-term average

At the bottom on Nov. 15, bitcoin traded about 8.5% under the 200-week average, a wider gap than the 7.3% recorded at June’s low of $58,500. K33 said 51.5% of the bitcoin supply last moved on-chain at prices above the current level, meaning the average holder could have sold for more at some point in the past four years.

Lunde said those readings, taken together, have typically lined up with market bottoms. K33 also noted that crypto has lagged traditional markets, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 recovering modestly last week while bitcoin sank.

Bitcoin was trading near $62,300 on Wednesday, according to Coinbase spot prices, below the roughly $65,000 level cited in the K33 report, which showed bitcoin down 14% on the week and about 20% over 30 days. Ether also fell 14% over the week, to around $1,827.

Outflows, liquidations and hedging

Capital continues to leave bitcoin funds. Net outflows from bitcoin exchange-traded products reached 44,900 BTC over the 14 trading days since Oct. 29, K33 said, short of the record of about 71,000 BTC set in June. Total ETF holdings fell to about 1.46 million BTC, the lowest since Aug. 19, and leveraged ETF exposure dropped to 21,900 BTC, the lowest since March 2024.

Forced selling hit derivatives, too. About $1.3 billion in long positions were liquidated on Nov. 13 and 14 as bitcoin broke below $70,000, K33 said, and funding rates on perpetual futures repeatedly turned negative. Open interest fell by about 30,000 BTC but stayed above 330,000 BTC, leaving leverage elevated against historical norms.

Institutional futures players largely stayed on the sidelines. Open interest in bitcoin futures on CME stayed below 100,000 BTC all week, K33 said, a sign that regulated-market participants have not rushed in to buy the dip.

Demand for downside protection is also surging. The one-month 25-delta skew, which compares the price of puts to calls, rose above 20 for the first time since July, a level Lunde said has historically coincided with “selling exhaustion near local bottoms.”

Stablecoins offer another sign of stress. K33 said net redemptions totaled $16.1 billion over the past month, the largest outflow since the collapse of Terra.

A bottom, but not a bounce

Lunde stopped short of calling the decline over. He said earlier recoveries from similar conditions involved “prolonged consolidation,” pointing to a choppy recovery rather than an immediate rebound.

There were some constructive signs in trading activity. Spot volume ran near $5 billion a day from Friday through Sunday, the busiest weekend since February, which K33 said could give the market firmer footing after weeks of one-way selling.

Even so, leverage remains high, and ETF money is still heading out the door. Bitcoin was near $62,300 at the time of writing, below the roughly $68,000 200-week average K33 flagged as a key level.

This post Analyst: Bitcoin Below $70,000 is a ‘Gift From the Market’ first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Pepe Meme Coin Likely to Provide Another Selling Opportunity as Bids Thin to $694K
description: PEPE fell about 30% in a week and trades near the bottom of its range. Thin Binance bids and negative funding put the $0.0000033 floor in focus.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • PEPE lost nearly a third of its value in a week, falling far harder than Bitcoin.
  • The daily chart keeps sellers in charge, with the token stuck below both key moving averages.
  • Traders are watching the floor near $0.0000033, where a break could open a deeper slide.

PEPE suffered one of its worst weeks in months, and the frog-themed token now trades close to the bottom of its recent range. Buy orders on Binance look thin next to the sell side.

That matters because the October breakout against Bitcoin has unraveled, and derivatives traders have turned bearish. Short sellers could still spark a squeeze. Traders now watch whether buyers defend support or sell into any bounce.

PEPE Sheds Nearly a Third of Its Value in a Week

PEPE traded near $0.0000038 on Nov. 18, down about 30% over seven days. That slide was far steeper than Bitcoin's move over the same stretch.

CoinGecko data puts the weekly range between roughly $0.000003662 and $0.000005298. The price now sits only about 3.8% above that low. In plain terms, PEPE is hugging the floor of its recent range.

The Binance PEPE/USDT order book shows why buyers look hesitant. About $975K in sell orders sits within 2% above the price. Only $694K in bids waits within the same distance below. Daily turnover runs near $25M, so a modest wave of selling could push through those thin bids.

How We Got Here

Late October looked very different. On Oct. 29, 2026, wallets linked to Justin Sun held about $51.25M of PEPE, based on on-chain data. At the same time, PEPE broke a two-year downtrend against Bitcoin. Traders read both signals as a sign of fresh demand.

That optimism did not last. The breakout failed, and the weekly slide wiped out the October gains. PEPE now sits about 6% lower over 30 days.

Derivatives traders turned bearish as the price fell. Funding on Binance 1000PEPE futures went negative, with open interest near $74M. That means short sellers are paying to hold their bets. Those shorts could fuel a squeeze, though no sign of one has appeared yet.

Sellers Keep PEPE Pinned Beneath Both Averages

Pepe (PEPE) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows PEPE trading below both of its key moving averages. The 50-day average sits near $0.0000043. The 200-day average sits near $0.0000040. Both lines now act as ceilings, so rallies must fight through them.

Momentum still points down, with MACD below its signal line. Trend gauges confirm that sellers lead the move. The token slipped about 1% over the last day, which suggests the selling has slowed without stopping.

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, reads 36. That reading is weak but sits above oversold territory. In practice, sellers still have room to push lower before the market looks stretched.

A move back to $0.000004 would be a first sign of improvement. The first real ceiling sits near $0.0000041, where a bounce will likely meet sellers. Beyond that, the 50-day line caps the price.

On the downside, the floor that matters sits slightly lower. A break there opens the way toward $0.0000025.

A Recovery Now Demands a 40% Climb

The weekly slide leaves PEPE holders facing steep math.

  • Long-term holders: Winning back the full weekly loss now takes a gain of about 42.9%. Even a return to the weekly high needs roughly 39.4%.
  • The project: October's breakout against Bitcoin has failed for now. With 420.69 trillion tokens in circulation, large wallets can weigh heavily on price if they sell.
  • Large holders: Sun-linked wallets face a test of conviction as their stake loses value.
  • Short-term traders: Negative funding could spark short covering, but none has shown up yet. Any bounce may work better as a chance to trim exposure.

Will PEPE Print a Higher Low Above Support?

The next few sessions should show whether the weekly low holds.

  • A higher low: A dip that stops above the weekly low would hint that buyers are stepping in.
  • Short covering: A squeeze only counts if price then holds above the first ceiling.
  • The bid side: Thicker bids would show real demand returning.

title: Fed Governor Sends Shockwave Through Markets With 50bp Rate Hike Call
description:
Stocks, gold, and Bitcoin fell as Fed's Waller called for a 50 basis point rate hike to break 3% inflation.
The post Fed Governor Sends Shockwave Through Markets With 50bp Rate Hike Call appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Stocks and gold fell on Wednesday after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller called for a 50-basis-point rate hike in December. Short-term Treasury yields and the dollar rose.

Waller wants the Fed’s first half-point hike since 2022. He says Americans may need a “shock” to stop treating 3% inflation as normal. That bill would land on borrowers, tech stocks, and Bitcoin holders.

How Did Markets React to Waller’s Call?

The two-year Treasury yield, which tracks where traders expect Fed rates to go, moved higher.

Gold dropped about 2% on the day to near $3,773 an ounce. Bitcoin slipped about 1.3%, TradingView chart shows.

Yet the 10-year yield barely moved, holding near 5.12%. Yields above 5% leave debt-heavy AI firms exposed. Meanwhile, traders are not buying the bigger hike. CME FedWatch still showed 95% odds of a quarter-point move.

Why Does the Fed Governor Want to Shock Americans?

Core prices, which skip food and energy, rose 0.3% for three months straight. That pace points to about 3.5% a year, against a 2% target.

About 70% of core services prices now climb faster than 3%, he said. None of it, he added, comes from oil.

“I’m very, very concerned about inflation. It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out,” he said.

He would accept a quarter-point hike only if the Fed promised another in January. He also wants the Fed’s three 2025 rate cuts reversed. Yet he sees nothing “bubble-like” in AI prices.

His colleagues are split:

  • St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem sees up to four hikes by spring 2027.
  • New York Fed President John Williams says dramatic action is not needed.

Economist Peter Schiff, a longtime Fed critic, asks whether the Fed will keep rescuing markets.

“Will the Fed choose to worsen the inflation problem to bail out investors again?” Schiff posed.

The Fed votes December 8–9. Wednesday’s minutes from its October meeting will show how many officials share Waller’s alarm.

title: US Treasury’s $6 Billion Bond Move Raises Red Flags for Bitcoin
description:
The US Treasury's $6 billion bond buyback filled just $1.18 billion. See what the miss means for yields and Bitcoin.
The post US Treasury’s $6 Billion Bond Move Raises Red Flags for Bitcoin appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
As borrowing money remains expensive in the US, its latest attempt to improve trading in government debt has delivered an unusually weak result. This could have a significant impact on an already weak crypto and stock market. 

On Tuesday, the US Treasury bought back far fewer bonds than its expanded program allows. The disappointing operation comes as Bitcoin falls toward $62,000 and investors worry about the direction of US interest rates.

What Happened With the US Treasury?

The US government regularly borrows money by selling bonds to investors. In return, it pays interest.

But some older bonds become difficult to trade. To keep the market running smoothly, the Treasury occasionally buys them back.

On November 17, it offered to purchase up to $6 billion of long-term bonds. Investors offered $4.55 billion, but the government accepted just $1.18 billion.

It was the smallest operation since the program expanded in September.

The weak result suggests a gap between what investors wanted and what the Treasury was willing to pay. It does not necessarily mean demand for US debt is collapsing.

Why Should Stock and Bitcoin Investors Care?

The bigger concern is that US borrowing costs remain high.

The 30-year Treasury yield stood at 5.46% on Tuesday. Higher yields can make mortgages and business loans more expensive. They also make government bonds more attractive compared with riskier investments, including stocks and Bitcoin.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin has dropped toward $62,000, roughly 20% below its price when Treasury announced the expanded buyback plan in September.

Some investors initially hoped larger buybacks would improve market liquidity and support crypto prices.

However, buybacks do not print new money. There is also no confirmed evidence linking Tuesday’s result directly to Bitcoin’s decline.

For now, high bond yields and continued Bitcoin ETF outflows remain more relevant market pressures.

The next signals to watch are Treasury yields, upcoming buybacks and Bitcoin ETF flows. Together, they will help show whether financial conditions are improving or becoming more difficult for investors.

title: Coinbase AI Thwarts Stops Elon Musk Crypto Scam, Blocking Millions of Stolen Funds
description: A deepfake Musk livestream promised to double viewers' crypto, but Coinbase's AI agent stopped 91% of attempted funds from reaching scammers.
fullContent:
Coinbase said its AI-powered scam detection system stopped $4.7 million, which is around 91% of the funds targeted by scammers, from reaching their wallets during a fake Elon Musk crypto giveaway.

What makes the incident stand out is that the entire operation was handled without human intervention, as the company’s AI agent identified the scam and stepped in as customers attempted to send their money.

The scheme revolved around a fraudulent YouTube livestream that appeared to show Tesla’s flying car demonstration.

Deepfake Crypto Scam

The fake livestream used an AI-generated version of Elon Musk, displayed crypto wallet addresses and a QR code, and promised viewers double their money if they sent cryptocurrency. More than 500,000 people watched the stream, giving the fake event plenty of exposure. According to Coinbase, the difficult part was that the scammers did not need to break into anyone’s account or steal login details.

Customers were logged in, had access to their funds, and willingly approved the transfers because they believed the giveaway was legitimate.

That makes this type of fraud harder to catch using traditional security measures, which generally focus on unauthorized account access or suspicious activity.

To address the problem, Coinbase deployed an AI scam-prevention agent designed to flag risky transfers and challenge customers before their money leaves the platform. The system uses machine learning models to assess transactions in real time. It looks for warning signs such as giveaway-related activity, brand impersonation, and transfers to newly created wallet addresses.

When a payment is flagged, the AI agent steps in with a targeted conversation that explains the specific scam pattern and why the offer should raise concerns, rather than relying on a generic security warning. Coinbase also said that every response generated by the agent receives a confidence score before being shown to the customer, which helps the system determine when it has enough information to intervene confidently.

Interestingly, the said crypto exchange agent had never encountered this particular scam before. Deepfake giveaways connected to live product launches were not part of its training, but it still recognized familiar warning signs, including promises to multiply crypto holdings, time pressure, and irreversible transfers. The system reportedly handled the flagged attempts from the first transaction to the last without requiring a human to step in.

“Before, staging a scam like this took a crew, a studio, and weeks. Now it takes a livestream slot and a model. Deepfakes make convincing scams cheap, fast, and easy to relaunch under a new name the moment one is shut down. That means our defenses have to improve at the same rate the attacks do. We’re investing heavily in AI across Risk to make that happen.”

Major Attack Vector

A Gartner survey of 297 senior cybersecurity leaders, conducted between March and May 2026 and published in September, found that 41% of CISOs had dealt with at least one social engineering incident involving an employee audio deepfake over the previous 12 months. Video deepfakes weren’t far behind. More than one in three CISOs, or 36%, said their organization had experienced this type of incident.

In June, Japanese crypto advocate Mai Fujimoto was tricked by a deepfake impersonating an acquaintance during a Zoom call, which eventually led to malware stealing access to her accounts. Binance founder CZ later warned that even video calls can no longer guarantee someone’s identity.

title: Why Bitcoin’s Order Book Can Fool You
description:
The short version Depth shows quantity, not how fast it changes. Book Churn counts price-level updates every ten minutes. Volatility […]
The post Why Bitcoin’s Order Book Can Fool You appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
The short version

  • Depth shows quantity, not how fast it changes.
  • Book Churn counts price-level updates every ten minutes.
  • Volatility hit rate: 63% against a 50% baseline.
  • A simple price-range signal matched it.

Glassnode’s November 18 research built the metric from Binance perpetual futures data, with Bitcoin and Ether backfilled to January 2020. The results hold up against random noise. They barely beat a far simpler measure.

What Book Churn actually counts

Binance streams every change to its order book as it happens. Each message says, in effect, that a given price now holds a new quantity of bids or asks. Trades trigger messages too, because a fill shrinks what rests at that price. Glassnode adds these messages up in ten-minute windows. On BTCUSDT, a typical window carries about 607,000.

A raw count needs context. Glassnode turns it into a score by measuring each window against the same clock hour over the previous 30 days, so a busy trading hour faces its own history and the dead of night faces its own. A score of 2 marks an unusually active window. Readings of 3 or more are rarer still.

The feed has blind spots. It reports price levels, not individual orders, so one message can bundle several cancels, new orders and fills. It doesn’t separate a pulled quote from an executed one, and it names no traders. When the exchange connection drops and resets, a window can even read quieter than it was. A spike tells you the book got busy. It can’t tell you why.

Two books, one screenshot

Picture two order books with identical quantities at every price. Same depth. Same spread. A screenshot can’t tell them apart, but ten minutes of watching can: in Glassnode’s illustration, one book changes 14 times and the other 56. Those counts are invented to show the idea. The point behind them is real. Depth tells you how much is resting, churn tells you how often it moves, and neither metric answers the other’s question.

April 27: the book barely flinched, the feed tripled

Depth here means the dollar value of bids and asks resting within 1% of the mid-price. The spread is the gap between the best bid and the best ask. On the morning of April 27, both looked calm.

Three windows starting at 05:10, 05:20 and 05:30 UTC carried 1.8 million to 2.1 million updates each, up from 0.6 million to 0.9 million in the hour before. Churn scores hit 4.34, 3.83 and 3.41. Combined depth, which had ranged between $400 million and $464 million in the prior hour, slipped to between $377 million and $412 million. Then it jumped to $565 million in the next window. The spread sat at about one tick throughout.

Price didn’t sit still. The high-to-low range reached 95 basis points, close to 1%, in the first burst window, then 28 and 39 basis points in the next two. Range shows how far price traveled inside a window, not which way it finished.

So a trader watching depth and spread saw a mild dip. Underneath, the update feed nearly tripled.

Most busy windows don’t look like this. Across BTCUSDT history, higher churn usually came with thinner depth and wider spreads, with correlations of -0.40 and +0.49 respectively. The case that matters most, with normal depth, quiet prices and frantic quoting all at once, showed up in only about 7% of BTCUSDT readings at 3 or above. Those are the windows where churn picks up something nothing else on the screen shows.

Keep the scope in mind. This is one perpetual futures contract on one exchange, not the whole Bitcoin market. And combined depth counts both sides of the book, so a buyer can only draw on the asks, a fraction of that total.

Where churn meets your fill

A market buy takes the cheapest ask first, then the next one up, and keeps climbing until the order is complete. Coinbase’s trading rules spell out that a single market order can fill at several prices. Here’s a made-up book, shown twice: once as you saw it, and once after a single quote moved.

Hypothetical asks, buying 3 BTC
Ask price Book A: as seen Book B: one quote moved
$100,000 1 BTC none
$100,100 1 BTC 1 BTC
$100,150 none 1 BTC
$100,200 3 BTC 3 BTC
Cost of 3 BTC $300,300 $300,450

In Book A, a 3 BTC market buy pays $100,000, $100,100 and $100,200, an average of $100,100 before fees. Anyone expecting the whole order at the top price pays $300 more than planned. Thin depth at the best ask did that. Churn played no part.

Book B is where churn comes in. The seller at $100,000 pulls that coin and reposts it at $100,150 a moment before your order lands. You see the same screen and send the same order, and you pay $450 above the top-of-book estimate. Repeat that kind of swap across thousands of price levels and you get a churn spike. The score can’t say which level will move, or where it goes next.

A limit order caps the price but may leave you partly filled, or not filled at all. Coindoo’s guide to how crypto orders execute covers that trade-off, and fees sit on top of every figure above, as our breakdown of Bitcoin buying costs shows.

63% sounds strong. The baseline is 50%.

Glassnode’s main test asked a narrow question. When churn scored 2 or higher, was the next hour more volatile than the median hour? Half of all hours land above the median by definition, so a coin flip scores 50%.

Share of signals followed by an above-median volatility hour. Source: Glassnode
Signal BTCUSDT ETHUSDT
Random placebo spikes 51.2% 50.5%
Churn reading from 24 hours earlier 58.9% 58.4%
Churn score 2 or higher 63.2% 63.4%
Price-range signal 63.7% 63.5%
Churn score 3 or higher 69.1% 68.2%

Start at the top. Random spikes land right on the coin flip, which tells you the test isn’t rigged. Churn clears that line, and higher scores clear it by more.

The highlighted row is the awkward one. Glassnode built a matching signal from nothing but each window’s high-to-low swing, and it edged churn by a fraction of a point, a gap too small to call either way. The two scores move together with a correlation of 0.84. Price range alone explains about 70% of the variation in the churn score. For the most part, churn re-measures price movement through the quote feed.

Not entirely, though. In roughly half the windows where churn fired, the range signal stayed silent. Similar accuracy, different moments.

The day-old row tells its own story. A reading from a full day earlier kept most of the edge, which points to volatility that lingers for days, while the current reading adds four to five points on top. And about 37% of high readings still came before a perfectly ordinary hour.

Glassnode lists its own limits. The test ran in-sample: volatility buckets and control groups were set using each full calendar year, including months a live trader wouldn’t have seen yet. Results for 2020 and 2021 came in at 53% to 57%, not clearly above chance. By Glassnode’s own description, Bitcoin and Ether on one exchange amount to close to a single test. The score says nothing about direction, and the study never measured trading returns or execution costs.

READ MORE:

XRP Ledger’s Big Bank Test Covered Only 2 of 10 Rules

Before you send a large order

Check the ask side at your own order size. A combined depth figure blends buyers and sellers, and the best price usually covers only the first slice of a big order.

During a churn spike, read a one-tick spread as a fact about the best price and nothing deeper. The next level up may be the one getting rewritten.

Then decide which risk you would rather carry. A market order gets the trade done at an unknown price. A limit order holds the price and may never fill.

Glassnode hasn’t tested whether churn improves real fills once depth, spread and fees enter the math. It also doesn’t publish how long each reading takes to arrive after its window closes, which matters to anyone hoping to act on one. What the metric does today is narrower and still worth having. When updates triple and the spread doesn’t budge, the calm you see is only the top layer.

title: Why AI-ROC Is the Future of Exposure Management
description: Executive Summary Security teams have never had better visibility into their assets, vulnerabilities, and threats. What they lack is the speed to act on it. Frontier AI models are surfacing vulnerabilities faster than ever, attackers are using the same models to exploit them within hours, and most remediation still depends on scans, tickets, and change […]
fullContent:
Executive Summary

Security teams have never had better visibility into their assets, vulnerabilities, and threats. What they lack is the speed to act on it. Frontier AI models are surfacing vulnerabilities faster than ever, attackers are using the same models to exploit them within hours, and most remediation still depends on scans, tickets, and change windows. Exposure management needs a new operating model that detects exposures as soon as they are disclosed, focuses only on what is proven exploitable, and remediates autonomously without breaking the business. That operating model is the AI-native Risk Operations Center (AI-ROC).

On October 13, 2026, Microsoft released the largest Patch Tuesday in its history, fixing 1,414 vulnerabilities. That is more than seven times the 193 vulnerabilities Microsoft fixed in October 2025. One of the new vulnerabilities was already being exploited, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) set a deadline of just three days to patch it.

At ROCon Americas 2026, we made the case that most organizations are focused on the wrong question. Knowing how many exposures you have is no longer useful on its own. What matters is how quickly you can turn those exposures into verified risk reduction.

The Vulnerability Surge Has Outpaced Remediation

Over the last twenty years, the security industry has gotten very good at finding things. Organizations now have more data on assets, vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, threat intelligence, and alerts than ever before. The ability to fix what matters has not kept up.

Frontier AI has made that gap much wider. These models are not creating new vulnerabilities. They are surfacing flaws that already existed in code, and they are doing it much faster than before. The last two Patch Tuesdays, with 974 vulnerabilities in September and more than 1,400 in October, show how fast this is moving. Attackers have access to the same AI tools and are using them to weaponize new vulnerabilities within hours. In September, two of the vulnerabilities Microsoft disclosed were already being exploited before a patch was available.

The way most organizations remediate has barely changed. A scanner detects the vulnerability, a second tool adds asset context, a third ranks it, an attack simulation tool tests it, and a ticket is created in the hope that someone fixes it within a 30- or 60-day service-level agreement (SLA). Each of those handoffs adds time, and risk only goes down when the fix is actually applied. This process was not built for attackers who move in hours.

What the Surge Means for Security Teams

Remediation timelines are shrinking from weeks to days, but the resources to meet them are not keeping pace.

  • SLAs are moving from weeks to days. The 30- and 60-day SLAs most programs were built around no longer match the threat. Critical vulnerabilities now need to be patched in days, and mandates from CISA and CERT-In, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team, can require remediation in as little as 12 to 24 hours.
  • Exploitation is how most breaches now start. The Verizon 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report found that vulnerability exploitation was the leading way attackers got in, while the median time to patch grew to 43 days.
  • Budgets and headcount are not keeping pace. Only 15% of security leaders expect their budgets to grow by more than 10%. Hiring more analysts is not a realistic answer.
  • There are too many findings to fix. One large Qualys customer had 62.5 million findings. No team has the time or budget to work through that many.

The Ideal Operating Model for Exposure Management

None of this is a new problem. Exposure management still comes down to the same basics of visibility, prioritization, and remediation. What has changed is the speed at which each of them has to happen.

  • Detection must happen in real time. New exposures should be identified as soon as a vulnerability is disclosed, not after the next scheduled scan.
  • Prioritization must be based on proof. Risk scores tell you what could be dangerous. Teams need to know whether an attacker can actually reach and exploit the vulnerability in their environment.
  • Remediation must take hours, not a month. Low-risk fixes should be automated, and every fix should be checked to confirm it worked.

These steps also need to run on one platform. Every handoff between separate tools and teams adds delay, and that delay is the window attackers use.

Qualys calls this operating model the Risk Operations Center (ROC). When AI agents handle the time-sensitive work at each stage, it becomes an AI-native ROC, or AI-ROC.

How Qualys Operationalizes the AI-ROC

The Qualys AI-ROC brings this operating model together on the Qualys Enterprise TruRisk Management Platform. It pulls in every asset and exposure across cloud, on-premises, operational technology (OT), Internet of Things (IoT), mobile, and AI environments, enriches them with threat intelligence and business context, and then prioritizes and remediates the risk that matters. Three AI agents handle the work that has to happen at machine speed: Agent Insta for detection, Agent Val for validation, and Agent Sara for remediation.

AI-Speed Detection with InstaScan

With traditional scanning, a vendor has to write a detection signature, roll it out, and then customers have to rescan their environment. That can take a day or two before a team even knows it is affected. InstaScan, powered by Agent Insta, monitors vendor advisories around the clock and matches them against the asset and software data customers already have. No new scan is needed. After the October release, Agent Insta customers had detections within five minutes.

Hyper-Prioritization with TruConfirm

Even after applying threat intelligence and business context, a large organization can still be left with hundreds of thousands of findings. TruConfirm, powered by Agent Val, tests whether those findings can actually be exploited in the customer’s environment, using production-safe payloads that never download malware. For the customer mentioned above, this reduced 62.5 million findings to 60,000 that were confirmed exploitable.

Zero-Day Remediation with TruRisk Eliminate

Detection and prioritization only matter if the risk gets fixed. Before launching TruRisk Eliminate with TruConfidence, we kept asking why teams were not remediating faster. Automation was not the blocker, since patch automation tools have existed for years. Confidence was. Teams did not know whether they were choosing the right fix, whether a patch would crash a business application, or whether compensating controls already covered the risk.

TruRisk Eliminate with TruConfidence is built to answer those questions and to be the system of record and system of action for cyber risk reduction. It takes prioritized findings from Qualys or third-party tools and recommends the right fix for each one. A patch reliability score shows how likely a patch is to deploy without issues, and integrations with firewalls and other controls show when a compensating control already covers the risk. Patching is not always the answer. If a company has moved from Zoom to Microsoft Teams and a Zoom zero-day is disclosed, the right action is to uninstall Zoom rather than patch it.

Agent Sara plans the rollout. Low-impact updates such as browsers and standalone utilities are patched automatically with no reboot required. Production workloads are patched in rings, starting in a lab environment, with health monitoring through partners like Dynatrace. If CPU, memory, or network indicators show a problem, Agent Sara stops the rollout and rolls the patch back. When a patch is not safe to deploy, Agent Sara applies a mitigation instead.

Trust Is Built Into the AI-ROC

As soon as agents start remediating, security and IT teams ask the same four questions. The AI-ROC answers each one with a setting the team controls.

  • What breaks if the agent gets it wrong? Every patch carries an AI reliability score based on real-world deployments. Dependency and downtime impact are known before anything is approved, and rollback is staged in advance.
  • Can we start small and prove it? Deployment waves let teams start with zero-touch automation for low-impact fixes, use ring-based rollouts for everything else, and keep tighter control over their most critical systems. Each team decides where to start.
  • How do I know why it did that? ROCky, the Qualys conversational AI interface, and every agent show their reasoning, including the threat, the affected asset, any compensating control, and the TruConfirm evidence behind each action.
  • Can I take the wheel back? Each wave can have its own approval gate. Rollback happens automatically if a service degrades, and nothing is marked closed until it has been revalidated.

Policy, risk appetite, confidence thresholds, approval gates, and exceptions stay with the security team, and the agents work within those boundaries. Autonomy is not something teams have to take on faith. They control how much of it to use, and the program can grow with the environment instead of with headcount.

How the Three Agents Handle a Zero-Day

At ROCon, we walked through how the agents worked together on CVE-2026-81963, a Windows vulnerability from the September Patch Tuesday that CISA added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on the same day. Agent Insta detected it in the customer’s environment within minutes of disclosure. Agent Val confirmed it was exploitable on the customer’s assets. Agent Sara saw that the patch required a reboot and already had a low reliability score, so it deployed to the lab environment first. When health indicators showed issues, Agent Sara rolled the patch back and applied a temporary mitigation, reducing the risk without the patch ever reaching production.

What Comes Next for the AI-ROC

Organizations can adopt the AI-ROC in stages. The journey begins with AI-speed detection, then extends CTEM across every tool already in use, moves to autonomous risk elimination, and finally quantifies cyber risk in business terms for the chief information security officer (CISO), the chief financial officer (CFO), and the board. Each stage builds on the one before it, so teams see results early while working toward a fully autonomous program.

The AI-ROC will continue to grow with the attack surface. As applications, AI systems, and more advanced attack techniques create new kinds of exposure, they will come into the same platform, the same risk view, and the same agent-driven workflows.

Agentic ROC Studio and the Future of Agentic AI in Risk Operations

The next step is Agentic ROC Studio, a concept Qualys is building toward. Every security team has its own runbooks, its own tools, and its own way of working, and no set of prebuilt agents can cover all of it. Agentic ROC Studio is designed to let teams build agents around how they already operate. A team would describe what an agent should do in plain language, choose the tools it is allowed to use, and have it running in minutes, with no scripting required.

These agents would work alongside the Qualys AI agents for exposure, threat, patch, and compliance, and connect to third-party tools and agents across security, IT, cloud, and identity to run as one cross-domain workflow. That is where agentic AI in risk operations is headed: a digital workforce that takes on the repetitive work across the entire risk program, while the security team sets the rules and stays in the loop.

Conclusion

Frontier AI has changed the pace of vulnerability management. Record Patch Tuesdays have arrived for two consecutive months; attackers can weaponize new flaws within hours, and the SLAs most programs were built on no longer hold. Adding more scanners, more findings, and more tickets will not close that gap.

What closes it is an operating model built for AI speed. That means detecting new vulnerabilities as soon as they are disclosed, proving which ones can be exploited, and remediating them autonomously with safeguards that let teams trust the results. The AI-ROC brings all of this together on one platform, with AI agents doing the work at machine speed and security teams in control of every decision that matters.

Every tool on the market can tell you how many exposures you have. The organizations that stay ahead in the frontier AI era will be the ones that can answer a harder question: how quickly can we turn exposure into verified risk reduction?

Ready to see how the Qualys AI-ROC detects, validates, and remediates exposures at AI speed? Watch the full session from ROCon Americas 2026, then try it in your own environment with a free 30-day trial of Qualys Enterprise TruRisk Management (ETM).

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What Is an AI-ROC?

An AI-native Risk Operations Center. It detects exposures as soon as they are disclosed, proves which are exploitable, remediates with guardrails, and revalidates before closure. Security teams set policy and stay in control.

What Do the Three Agents Do?

Agent Insta handles detection. Agent Val handles validation. Agent Sara handles remediation, including reliability scoring, ring rollouts, and rollback.

Can the Agents Patch Without Approval?

Only within the boundaries the team sets. Low-impact updates can be zero-touch. Each wave can have its own approval gate. Rollback is automatic if a service degrades. Nothing is marked closed until it has been revalidated.

What Is Agentic ROC Studio?

How Fast Does InstaScan Detect?

It matches new advisories against the asset and software data customers already have, so no new scan is required. After the October 2026 release, Agent Insta customers had detections within five minutes.

title: ADA Foundation CEO Says No One Decides When Cardano Is Finished as Price Sits at $0.15
description: Cardano Foundation CEO Frederik Gregaard pushed back on roadmap talk as ADA slid near $0.15. Traders watch the $0.12 floor while RSI signals oversold.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • Cardano Foundation CEO Frederik Gregaard defended the network's future after Charles Hoskinson called the original roadmap complete.
  • ADA looks deeply oversold, yet momentum still favors sellers.
  • Traders are watching whether buyers defend the floor near $0.12.

Cardano's foundation is pushing back on the idea that the network's work is done. Its chief said no single person decides when Cardano is finished, and his team filed a new treasury request to fund conferences.

The timing is tough for ADA holders. The token has slid for weeks, and the budget assumes a price the market has already left behind. Traders now want to know if adoption talk can stop the selling.

Gregaard Pushes Back on the Roadmap Backlash With a $5M Ask

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson set off a backlash this month when he declared the network's original roadmap complete. He later clarified that he meant the original engineering roadmap. Development continues, he said, and so does his own involvement.

Gregaard answered critics in a Nov. 15 statement. "Decentralization means that no single individual gets to decide when Cardano is finished," he said. He pointed to the Amaru and Dingo alternative nodes, written in Rust and Go, and to ADA futures on CME Group. He also cited the CIP-0113 token standard, which was used to tokenize 850,000 Veridian shares under Swiss law.

Gregaard also conceded a gap. Cardano must turn its initiatives into "production deployments, recurring transactions and sustainable economic activity," he said.

A day later, the Foundation filed a treasury proposal for 24,995,775 ADA. That is about $5M at an assumed $0.20 per token. The money would fund 12 conferences in 2027, including four hackathons. Sponsorships take about $2M and exhibition infrastructure $1M. Travel support gets $702K and side events $695K.

The prior program logged 8,191 booth contacts and 1,169 developers. It also recorded 219 potential collaborations and 1,045 wallet registrations. The new goals call for 9,520 contacts and 955 developers, with fewer collaborations than last time. The plan sets no target for on-chain transactions, the very metric Gregaard said matters most.

ADA Trades Well Below the Price the Foundation Budgeted On

Cardano (ADA) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

ADA traded near $0.15 on Monday, down about 3% on the day. The token sits below its 50-day average near $0.19. It also trades well under its 200-day average near $0.23. A moving average tracks the mean closing price over that many days. When price stays under both, each one acts as a ceiling, and the trend points down on short and long horizons alike.

That gap matters for the treasury request. The number of ADA in the proposal is fixed, so the dollar value it funds shrinks as the price falls. At current levels, the same tokens would cover noticeably less of the conference budget than planned.

The decline has also been steady. ADA lost about 14% over the past week and roughly 32% over the past month. Those figures point to persistent selling across several weeks, with no single crash day behind them.

ADA briefly touched a low near $0.148 on Nov. 14, the day before Gregaard's statement. It has hovered just above that mark since. The defense of the roadmap and the new spending plan have so far done little to bring buyers back.

The market is weighing the same shortfall Gregaard named. Cardano has plenty of initiatives and too little recurring activity on chain.

Oversold Readings Have Not Yet Stopped the Sellers

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 28 on the daily chart. Readings below 30 count as oversold. That often means selling has run ahead of itself, and relief bounces tend to start from zones like this one.

Oversold is a warning sign for sellers. It does not guarantee a turn. MACD, a tool that compares short and longer price averages, remains below its signal line, so momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings also show a real trend, and sellers are the ones leading it.

In a strong downtrend, RSI can stay pinned in oversold territory for weeks.

Traders looking for a bounce will want to see momentum turn first. A MACD cross above its signal line would be the earliest hint that buyers are stepping back in. Until then, the low RSI reading mostly measures how hard sellers have pushed.

Support sits near $0.12 on the daily chart. Below that level, the data shows no mapped floor at all. A clean break would leave ADA in open air, with no recent buying zone to slow the slide.

Buyers who stepped in there before would need to show up again. If they do not, the oversold reading could stretch further.

On the upside, the first hurdle stands near $0.18. That resistance sits just under the 50-day line. A daily close above both would be the first sign the downtrend is easing.

Beyond that, the next ceiling lines up with the price the treasury proposal assumed. Reclaiming it would restore the budget's full dollar value. For now, that level looks far off.

What Flips the Next Three Days

Two paths stand out, and each hinges on a level already in play.

  • Bullish: An oversold bounce that closes above the first hurdle under the 50-day line would open a run toward the price the treasury budget assumed. A slip back below the Nov. 14 low would cancel that setup.
  • Bearish: A break of the Nov. 14 low would likely send ADA down to test the floor bulls must defend. A daily close back above that first hurdle would invalidate the bearish case.

Adoption Must Show Up On Chain Before Price Does

The trend stays bearish until ADA reclaims that first resistance level. More booth contacts and developer sign-ups will not move the chart. Recurring transactions on chain might.

Short sellers face their own risk. Oversold markets can snap higher fast when crowded bets unwind, even inside a broader downtrend.

WASHINGTON—Sporting a puka-shell choker as he addressed the roomful of hastily summoned journalists, President Donald Trump held an emergency press conference Tuesday to explain that ohana means “family” in Hawaiian culture. “Ohana is about loyalty to all the people close to you, not just your blood relatives, and no one ever gets left behind,” said the commander-in-chief, draping an orchid lei around the neck of a CNN journalist, which he claimed represented the “aloha spirit.” “Mahalo is another word. It means ‘thank you,’ but has a bunch of other definitions most mainlanders have never even heard of. For those unfamiliar, Hawaii’s an island, but it’s also an American state. Home to the big guy who sings ‘Over The Rainbow’ and the blue extraterrestrial Stitch. Shaka brah.” At press time, Trump had reportedly cut off all federal aid to Hawaii after accusing the volcano goddess Pele of not being very nice to him.

title: Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout
Ionic Digital sold about 737 bitcoin for roughly $61.6 million after Sept. 30 and plans to use the cash to develop its data center sites, its latest quarterly report shows.
This post Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout

Ionic Digital (IOND) sold about 737 bitcoin after the end of September for roughly $61.6 million and plans to spend the money building out its data center sites, the miner built from Celsius’ old mining business disclosed in its latest quarterly report. The company said in its 10-Q that the coins sold at an average of $83,600 each, net of trading costs. The sales cut its bitcoin holdings by about 25% from the Sept. 30 balance.

Ionic held 2,954 bitcoin at the end of the third quarter, up from 2,719 at the end of 2025. That implies about 2,217 bitcoin left after the sales. “The Company intends to use the proceeds to fund the development of its existing data center sites,” the filing said.

The filing does not say when the coins were sold. Bitcoin traded near $64,000 on Wednesday morning, about 23% below Ionic’s average sale price.

From Celsius miner to landlord

Ionic was formed in January 2024 to take over the assets of Celsius Mining under the bankrupt lender’s Chapter 11 plan. It started out as a pure bitcoin miner, running fleets of ASIC machines at its own and hosted sites. That changed in October 2025, when it signed a lease with a single tenant for its Ward County, Texas, facility, which it previously called Cedarvale. The lease runs through January 2037.

The third quarter shows how far the shift has gone, with revenue rising to about $49.0 million from $37.1 million a year earlier. Digital infrastructure leasing brought in $43.9 million of that, while mining revenue fell to $5.1 million from $37.1 million.

Ionic swung to a net profit of $17.4 million for the quarter, compared with a $4.5 million loss a year earlier. That result included a $73.2 million gain on the fair value of its bitcoin, offset in part by a $65.9 million loss from remeasuring warrants. For the first nine months of the year, Ionic posted a net loss of $30.9 million.

More capacity for the tenant

In February, Ionic amended the Ward County lease. The tenant is now obligated to lease another 89 megawatts of capacity when it becomes available. Control of that added capacity had not passed to the tenant by the end of September, so Ionic has not booked any revenue on it. The company also had about $19.6 million left to pay on transformer purchases and a substation expansion at the site.

The conversion has cost Ionic mining capacity. The company said it does not have room at its owned and leased sites to relocate all of the miners it used to run, so it has decommissioned some of them. Ionic went public through a direct listing on July 28 and raised $400 million in a private placement before $16.7 million in costs. It had about $381.4 million in cash and equivalents at Sept. 30.

A familiar trade

Ionic is one of several public miners turning bitcoin into cash for AI and data center projects this month. MARA sold 13,597 bitcoin for $1.1 billion and said more sales were coming. Core Scientific plans to exit bitcoin mining by year-end, and Hyperscale Data sold its last bitcoin to fund an AI data center.

Ionic’s sale is smaller, but the share is large. A quarter of its treasury is now going into the data center buildout. The company still mines. In July, it moved its hashrate from Foundry to Luxor’s mining pool, and mining added about $5.1 million worth of bitcoin to its holdings in the third quarter.

The test now is whether the 89 megawatts come online fast enough to justify selling coins that would fetch about $14 million less at Wednesday’s price.

This post Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Peltola win doesn't end DOJ scrutiny of Alaska Senate race, officials say
description:
Democrat Mary Peltola was declared the victor in Alaska’s Senate race Tuesday, but Justice Department officials say their interest in the contentious campaign has not waned. 
A criminal grand jury investigation remains underway into whether Peltola staffers or others recruited a spoiler candidate with a similar name to incumbent Dan S. Sullivan (R) in an effort to confuse voters - allegations Peltola has denied.
Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. 
In a parallel civil case, the Justice Department continues to appeal a federal judge’s ruling last month denying the agency’s extraordinary request to delay certification of the vote over concerns the outcome could be tainted by that potential effort to siphon efforts away from the incumbent.
“The priority of investigating a criminal potential fraud doesn’t stop because of the election, no matter who wins or loses,” Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters last week. 
When asked whether his department would drop those legal battles if Peltola took a significant lead, Blanche added: “No. That investigation remains where it was, which means I’m not going to talk about it.”
Still, after a flurry of activity on both legal fronts in the run-up to Election Day, there have been few public signs of progress since the Nov. 3 vote. After the race was called late Tuesday evening, a Justice Department spokesperson said the agency stands by Blanche’s earlier remarks. 
Peltola has denied any involvement in a scheme to confuse voters. The other Sullivan on the ballot - retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan - has repeatedly maintained his candidacy was legitimate.
He ultimately netted fewer than 5,000 votes, less than half the more than 12,000-vote lead Peltola secured over her Republican opponent. 
Democrats have condemned both the civil suit and the criminal investigation as a norm-shattering effort by the Justice Department to influence the election’s outcome. 
Michael J. Heyman, the U.S. attorney in Alaska, took the unusual step of confirming the existence of the grand jury investigation, which had been underway since the summer, at a news conference five days before the election. 
Such probes are typically carried out in secret and Justice Department guidelines typically advise prosecutors from taking investigative steps before an election that could be seen as a sign of political bias. 
Though Heyman declined to discuss details of the probe, The Washington Post has reported that prosecutors have issued dozens of subpoenas and sent target letters and document preservation warnings to those it believes might have been involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan.
Among the recipients was Marc Elias, a prominent Democratic voting rights and election lawyer, whose firm represented Peltola’s campaign. A lawyer at the firm, whose text messages were quoted in a New York Times story, documenting the alleged recruitment effort also received a target letter, according to a person familiar with the matter who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss details of the ongoing probe.
Elias dismissed those warnings as the latest attempt by the Justice Department to target President Donald Trump’s political enemies.
The Justice Department’s civil suit was filed just weeks before the vote and as early voting was underway. Department lawyers had asked the court to suspend certification, in the event of a narrow Republican loss, until an investigation could be carried out into whether the outcome had been tainted. 
In her Nov. 1 ruling dismissing the case, U.S. District Judge Sharon L. Gleason said she had no authority to order such a probe and noted the department had offered no suggestion as to how such an investigation could be carried out while respecting the secrecy of voters’ ballot choices. 
The department immediately appealed Gleason’s ruling to the San Francisco-based U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit, which has so far shown no sign of taking up the matter quickly. 
The court has set a briefing schedule for arguments that extends until Jan. 11 - more than a week after Peltola is expected to be sworn in. 
The Justice Department has not asked to accelerate that schedule or moved to withdraw its case. 
Richard L. Hasen, a prominent election law scholar at UCLA, urged the appellate judges not to let the matter linger in a “friend of the court” brief filed Friday.
“This Court should send a swift and clear message to the federal government and the country,” Hasen wrote in the filing, “that the State of Alaska, and Alaska alone, has the right to certify the winner of its elections.”
Patrick Marley contributed to this report.
         
Related Content
This article originally appeared on Washington Post at https://washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/11/17/peltola-win-doesnt-end-doj-scrutiny-alaska-senate-race-officials-say/
